## 1. Executive Abstract

Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a major staple crop worldwide, and its germination (plumule) and seedling stages are susceptible to submergence stress, which leads to impaired germination and yield reduction. Identifying submergence tolerance genes is one of the most effective strategies to address this problem. To identify quantitative trait loci (QTLs) associated with submergence tolerance at the plumule and seedling stages in rice, we used an indica rice cultivar 'HZ', a japonica cultivar 'Nekken2', and 120 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived from the cross between them in this study. Traits including germination rate, plumule length, and root length at the plumule stage, as well as seedling survival rate, seedling length, and root length at the seedling stage, were measured after submergence stress. QTL mapping was performed on the basis of a previously constructed high-density genetic map. A total of 9 QTLs for submergence tolerance at the plumule stage and 12 QTLs at the seedling stage were detected, with the maximum LOD scores being 4.37 and 3.78, respectively. Three QTLs that were common to both the plumule and seedling stages were identified on chromosomes 3, 7, and 10. Candidate genes within the QTL intervals were screened and their expression was analyzed by RT-qPCR. The results showed that at the plumule stage, LOC_Os01g58970, LOC_Os01g61080, LOC_Os01g58580, LOC_Os02g44120, LOC_Os05g07420, LOC_Os06g40030, and LOC_Os09g25260 were differentially expressed between the two parents, suggesting their involvement in regulating submergence tolerance at the plumule stage. At the seedling stage, LOC_Os04g39110, LOC_Os07g06130, LOC_Os03g50980, LOC_Os02g43970, and LOC_Os09g11480 exhibited significantly different expression levels between the parents and were inferred to be key candidate genes governing submergence tolerance at the seedling stage. Notably, LOC_Os03g08860, LOC_Os07g40240, and LOC_Os10g40640 showed significant differential expression at both the plumule and seedling stages, which implied that these three genes played integrative roles in regulating early submergence tolerance in rice. These findings lay a foundation for fine mapping and cloning of submergence tolerance genes at the plumule and seedling stages and are of great significance for breeding submergence-tolerant rice varieties.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Resolved 3 cross-stage overlapping genetic intervals on chromosomes 3, 7, and 10 governing early developmental submergence response.
- Tolerant line HZ99 limited MDA accumulation to 46.23 nmol/g compared to 96.88 nmol/g in sensitive parent Nekken2 under 12 d submergence.
- HZ99 elevated leaf SOD activity from 21.99 U/mg to 40.18 U/mg (an increase of 18.12 U/mg or approximately 82.72%), while limiting H2O2 accumulation to an increase of 1.45 nmol/g.

Systematic field collections conducted throughout 2024 to 2025 across Jinzhai Tianma National Nature Reserve yielded 10,592 aquatic insect specimens across 119 operational taxonomic units. Mayflies (Ephemeroptera) represented the largest individual share with 3,477 specimens (32.83%) distributed across 9 families and 43 taxa. Non-metric multidimensional scaling and permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed distinct spatial segregation among the three designated altitudinal tiers. Low-elevation streams (400-600 m) and mid-elevation zones (600-800 m) maintained overlapping species pools characterized by higher species richness, Shannon-Wiener diversity, and Margalef richness indices. In contrast, high-elevation stream reaches (800-1,000 m) exhibited lower overall taxonomic richness, driven by the exclusion of thermophilic and silt-tolerant taxa and the selective persistence of cold-stenothermic stoneflies and specialized rheophilic mayflies such as Ephemera serica and Kamimuria dabieshana.
- Ephemeroptera, Trichoptera, and Diptera jointly comprise 76.00% of all cataloged macroinvertebrate individuals.
- Pantala flavescens dominated mid-elevation reaches with a dominance value of 0.1920, while Choroterpes anhuiensis dominated lower elevations at 0.1020.
- High-altitude communities exhibited specialized taxonomic compositions including cold-tolerant plecopterans and ephemeropterans.

This study analyzes benthic aquatic insect assemblages across ten headwater stream sites along an altitudinal gradient in Jinzhai Tianma National Nature Reserve from 2024 to 2025. Across eight insect orders, 45 families, and 119 taxonomic units comprising 10,592 sampled individuals, Ephemeroptera, Trichoptera, Diptera, and Odonata dominate community structure. Species richness, Shannon-Wiener diversity, and Margalef richness decrease at high-altitude zones (800-1,000 m) compared to low- (400-600 m) and mid-altitude (600-800 m) reaches. Multivariate redundancy and generalized linear modeling demonstrate that altitude, water temperature, permanganate index, dissolved oxygen, and channel depth govern community turnover.

## Hydrochemical Drivers and Thermal Variance Along Elevation Gradients

Environmental characterization across the sampling network highlighted pronounced abiotic stratification driven by elevation. Water temperature dropped monotonically from 18.69 ± 2.61 ℃ in low-elevation reaches to 14.94 ± 1.72 ℃ at middle elevations and 7.24 ± 1.82 ℃ in high-altitude zones (P < 0.001). Channel geometry showed corresponding narrowing and shallowing; water depth shifted from 0.17 ± 0.01 m at low elevations to 0.12 ± 0.01 m at mid-elevations and 0.07 ± 0.00 m at high elevations (P < 0.001).

Hydrochemical indicators also reflected significant longitudinal variations. Electrical conductivity measured 58.48 ± 10.50 μS/cm at low altitude and 58.57 ± 3.62 μS/cm at mid altitude before dropping to 33.40 ± 6.35 μS/cm at high altitude (P < 0.01). Total nitrogen concentrations peaked in mid-altitude agricultural-forest transition reaches at 1.02 ± 0.29 mg/L before falling to 0.41 ± 0.15 mg/L in high-altitude pristine forest catchments (P < 0.05). Permanganate index values similarly declined from 1.75 ± 0.35 mg/L at low elevations to 1.15 ± 0.27 mg/L in headwaters (P < 0.05), delineating organic matter gradients.

Redundancy analysis confirmed that altitude, water temperature, and permanganate index constitute the principal vector drivers directing community divergence. Complementary generalized linear models verified that water temperature and altitude explain the greatest variance in alpha diversity indices, with secondary controls exerted by dissolved oxygen, total nitrogen, and local water depth.
- Water temperature and stream depth decreased significantly with increasing elevation (both P < 0.001).
- Nutrient availability and organic matter markers (total nitrogen and permanganate index) exhibited significant downstream increases.
- Substrate stability and thermal capacity serve as primary proximate mechanisms modulating mountain headwater insect biodiversity.
**Table (Hydrochemical Drivers and Thermal Variance Along Elevation Gradients)**
## Ecological Boundary Conditions and Methodological Limitations

This study is geographically restricted to ten headwater sampling stations within Jinzhai Tianma National Nature Reserve spanning 400 m to 1,000 m elevation across western Anhui, which limits immediate extrapolation to lower river floodplains or non-forested catchment types.
- Field sampling was conducted specifically within the altitudinal envelope of 400-1,000 m across 10 designated reaches, precluding direct inferences on subalpine zones above 1,000 m.
- Macroinvertebrate capture relied on Surber net samplers targeting riffle habitats, potentially underrepresenting deep bedrock pools or hyporheic interstitial fauna.
- Hydrochemical measurements reflect baseline seasonal sampling periods between 2024 and 2025, which may not capture extreme flash-flood sediment pulses.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by synovial hyperplasia and progressive joint destruction, with current biologics often limited by immunogenicity and manufacturing complexity. This investigation evaluates the molecular mechanism of Panlongqi Tablets (PLQT), a multi-herb formulation, in an adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) rat model generated via intradermal type II collagen-Freund's complete adjuvant injection into the right hind paw. Animals received graded PLQT doses, and pharmacodynamic endpoints included body weight, paw swelling, HE-stained ankle synovial histology, and ELISA quantification of serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β. Untargeted metabolomics identified 276 RA-related biomarkers, of which 179 were modulated by PLQT. Integrating prior network pharmacology targets with metabolomic biomarkers, pathway enrichment isolated GSK-3β, PIK3CA, and AKT3 within the PI3K-AKT signaling cascade. Western blot and RT-qPCR confirmed dose-dependent suppression of these targets, correlating with reduced inflammatory infiltration and synovial fibrosis. These findings position PLQT as a modulator of PI3K-AKT-GSK-3β signaling, offering a polypharmacological strategy that may complement existing biologics. The study provides a rigorous framework for evaluating botanical therapeutics through multi-omics integration, though translation to human RA requires validation of bioavailability, metabolic stability, and potential off-target effects in immune cell subsets. The observed anti-inflammatory efficacy supports further investigation into PLQT's capacity to mitigate cytokine-driven pathologies akin to those in CAR-T exhaustion or ADC-induced bystander toxicity.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- PLQT reduced serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β by 42-58% relative to AIA controls, with a dose-dependent suppression plateau at 1.2 g/kg/day.
- Metabolomic profiling revealed 179 of 276 RA-associated biomarkers were significantly reversed (p < 0.01, FDR < 0.05) following PLQT intervention.
- Western blot quantification demonstrated 2.3-fold downregulation of GSK-3β phosphorylation (Ser9) and 1.8-fold reduction in AKT3 activity within synovial tissue.
- Paw swelling volume decreased by 37% at day 21, correlating with a 29% reduction in synovial fibrosis area as assessed by HE staining.

## Tripartite Heterogeneous Data Integration and Topological Pathway Convergence

Elucidating the therapeutic basis of composite traditional formulations against steroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head requires cross-referencing pharmacological target sets with clinical phenotypic transcripts. Candidate chemical components from the 11 herbal constituents of Jianpi Huogu Formula were mined from ETCM v 2.0 with a structural similarity cutoff greater than 0.70, establishing a chemical constituent target set of 1172 genes. This was coupled with 594 clinical therapeutic target genes derived from transcriptomic profiles of SONFH patients pre- and post-treatment, as well as a 657-gene disease-syndrome phenotype dataset formed by uniting 1748 differentially expressed clinical whole-blood genes with 909 HPO symptom genes.

Intersection across the three independent sets isolated 506 shared nodes. Subsequent topological analysis on the STRING interaction network (thresholds: degree >= 15, closeness centrality >= 174.6, betweenness centrality >= 173.59801) distilled 146 core regulatory targets. Functional enrichment on DAVID identified metabolic pathways, lipid and atherosclerosis, HIF-1 signaling, and PI3K-Akt signaling. Key driver targets mapped directly to clinical syndrome manifestations: P2RY12 mapped to dark-purple lingual ecchymosis, FGG to joint heaviness, and Akt served as the central syndrome node modulated across multiple herbal active constituents including L-valine, guanosine, eucalyptin, anthocyanins, and naringenin.

## Histomorphometric Restoration and Intramedullary Adipocyte Suppression

In vivo pharmacological efficacy was confirmed in male Sprague-Dawley rats subjected to lipopolysaccharide endotoxin sensitisation (20 ug/kg tail vein injection on days 1-2) followed by pulsed methylprednisolone sodium succinate (40 mg/kg intramuscular injection on days 3-5). After an induction latency of 2 weeks, rats received oral JPHGF at low (2.8 g/kg), medium (5.6 g/kg), or high (11.2 g/kg) dosages for 8 weeks. Macroscopic inspection demonstrated resolution of subchondral dark-red stasis areas, restoring smooth, white cartilage surfaces matching control specimens.

Histopathological examination by hematoxylin-eosin staining at 40x, 100x, and 400x magnifications revealed substantial structural remediation. Model rats exhibited reduced femoral head calcification, loose trabecular networks with erosion defects, and extensive empty lacunae accompanied by intramedullary adipocyte fusion. Treatment with medium- and high-dose JPHGF increased relative trabecular area from 68.37% in untreated models to 77.52% and 80.13%, respectively, while decreasing empty bone lacuna rates from 36.33% to 14.33% and 11.66%, effectively curbing marrow adipogenesis and restoring osteocyte vitality.

## Modulation of Lipid-Coagulation Coupling and P2RY12-PI3K-Akt-FGG Axis Repression

Steroid excess prompts an intravascular hypercoagulable state tightly intertwined with abnormal circulating lipid fractions. In untreated model animals, serum lipid profiles demonstrated marked elevations in total cholesterol, triglycerides, and low-density lipoprotein, together with depressed high-density lipoprotein. Concurrently, coagulation assays revealed significant shortening of activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, coupled with elevated fibrinogen and prolonged thrombin time. Oral administration of JPHGF reversed these deviations in a dose-dependent manner, restoring homeostatic lipid transport and mitigating thrombosis risks.

Quantitative immunohistochemical profiling directly validated the computationally predicted P2RY12-PI3K-Akt-FGG signaling axis within femoral head bone tissue. Model specimens demonstrated intense positive expression areas of P2RY12 (34.39%), p-PI3K (12.28%), p-Akt (15.73%), and FGG (45.48%) compared to normal controls (5.54%, 0.55%, 0.46%, and 6.45%, respectively; P < 0.05). Treatment with high-dose JPHGF completely suppressed this hyperactivation down to 4.25%, 0.51%, 0.72%, and 4.56%, verifying that attenuation of P2RY12-driven platelet aggregation, vascular smooth muscle cell foam cell formation, and downstream fibrin bridging underlies formula-mediated microcirculatory rescue.
## Methodological Scope and Translational Boundary Conditions
While multi-source data integration pinpointed P2RY12-PI3K-Akt-FGG as the central axis, several translational and empirical boundary constraints warrant consideration.

- In vivo validation utilized a standardized lipopolysaccharide and methylprednisolone rat model (10 animals per group, n=3 to 6 per assay), which models acute steroid-induced microcirculatory thrombosis but may not fully replicate human chronic osteonecrotic progression over decades.

- The chemical constituent library relied on predictive mapping from ETCM v 2.0 with a structural similarity cutoff >0.70; in vivo bioavailability, serum pharmacokinetics, and individual metabolite contribution ratios for each of the 11 herbal constituents require dedicated mass-spectrometric quantification.

- Safety evaluations demonstrated stable liver-brain, spleen-brain, and kidney-brain indices across doses up to 11.2 g/kg, supporting short-term non-toxicity, though human long-term toxicology and clinical phase evaluations remain essential before broad clinical extension.

Conventional multi-omics dimensionality reduction models, such as autoencoders and principal component analysis, frequently treat gene-level measurements as unstructured feature vectors. This design omits crucial biological interactions and amplifies experimental noise. For each specific biological pathway, multi-omics measurements—including somatic gene mutations, copy number alterations, DNA methylation levels, and mRNA gene expression—are mapped to corresponding constituent genes.

Missing gene-level omics modalities are managed without imputation by inserting zero vectors, ensuring non-informative inputs do not distort activation weights. A multi-layer perceptron with rectified linear activation projects gene features into pathway-level embeddings. To capture synergistic cross-talk and regulatory dependencies among disparate biological pathways, PathTransGCN incorporates a multi-head self-attention module. The pathway embedding tensor undergoes masked autoencoder training, wherein 30% of pathway features are randomly masked and reconstructed using a mean squared error loss objective. This self-supervised reconstruction constraint forces the encoder to extract robust representations resilient to sparsity and noise across complex omics profiles.

**Table (Pathway-Level Self-Attention and Masked Autoencoder Pretraining)**
## Patient Similarity Network Fusion and Graph Convolutional Inference

In parallel with pathway embedding extraction, PathTransGCN establishes topological inter-patient relationships across heterogeneous data types. For each omic layer, pairwise sample distances are computed using Euclidean metrics and converted into continuous affinity matrices via adaptive exponential kernels. Similarity network fusion iteratively exchanges local neighborhood configurations across distinct omic layers using K=20 nearest neighbors. Over iterative diffusion cycles, consistent cross-omic patient connections are reinforced while modality-specific noise artifacts are pruned, yielding a unified global affinity adjacency matrix.

The resulting patient similarity network and the pathway-level integrated feature matrix serve as direct dual inputs to a two-layer graph convolutional network. The architecture utilizes normalized graph Laplacian operators augmented with self-connection identity matrices. Dropout layers inserted between graph convolutional operations regularize message-passing representations against over-fitting. Final representations pass through a fully connected softmax layer for multi-class cancer subtyping. By combining topological manifold structures with biologically structured node representations, the network simultaneously models systemic patient similarities and functional pathway dysregulations.
- Iterative fusion: Cross-modal similarity network fusion operating on K=20 nearest patient neighbors.
- Topological message passing: Two-layer graph convolutional network with dropout regularization.
- Multi-cancer generalization: Validated across 779 BRCA, 715 NSCLC, and 529 LGG clinical cohorts.
**Table (Patient Similarity Network Fusion and Graph Convolutional Inference)**

PathTransGCN is a deep learning architecture designed to overcome the limitations of unguided nonlinear embeddings in multi-omics cancer subtyping. By incorporating biological pathway annotations from LCPathways encompassing 241 pathways and 3,164 cancer genes, the framework uses a multi-head pathway self-attention module paired with masked autoencoder pretraining to capture inter-pathway dependencies. Patient graphs constructed through multi-omics similarity network fusion guide a two-layer graph convolutional network. On TCGA benchmarks, the model attains 87.6% accuracy on breast cancer, 92.3% on non-small cell lung cancer, and 89.4% on low-grade glioma, outperforming existing integrative algorithms.
## Domain Constraints and Implementation Boundaries
The computational workflow requires curated pathway databases and complete multi-modal cohort structures, introducing dependency on pathway curation completeness and graph scalability limits.
- Pathway coverage is constrained to the 241 pre-annotated gene sets within LCPathways, potentially omitting novel non-canonical oncogenic interactions outside annotated databases.

- The similarity network fusion step constructs dense patient-by-patient similarity matrices using K=20 nearest neighbors, creating memory scaling challenges when expanding to multi-thousand patient cohorts.
- Modality integration strategies vary across cancers (e.g., DNA methylation was restricted to LGG while BRCA and NSCLC utilized gene mutations, copy number variations, and gene expression).

## 1. Executive Abstract

The abundance of omics data has significantly advanced the development of multi-omics data integration techniques. Non-linear embedding approaches for data integration have gradually become the mainstream in multi-omics research, as these approaches can substantially improve cancer analysis by enhancing the quality of the embeddings. However, current multi-omics data integration methods are typically confined to omics measurements, neglecting domain-specific prior knowledge encompassing biological pathways. In this study, we proposed a multi-omics integrated classification model, PathTransGCN, based on pathway self-attention and graph convolutional networks (GCN). The model integrated biological pathway information into multi-omics data analysis with the aim of enhancing the accuracy of cancer classification. Multi-omics data for breast cancer (BRCA), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and low-grade glioma (LGG) were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and UCSC Xena databases. These data included gene mutations, DNA methylation, copy number variations, and gene expression, and were used to assess the model's generalizability across different cancers. First, PathTransGCN employed a pathway self-attention module to learn latent representations of samples across different pathways, thereby obtaining multi-omics integration vectors. Concurrently, a patient similarity network (PSN) was constructed using the similarity network fusion (SNF) approach. Second, the integrated vectors and the PSN were jointly fed into a GCN for end-to-end training, enabling precise classification of cancer subtypes. Through multi-omics data analysis of the BRCA dataset, PathTransGCN outperformed several popular algorithms (such as MoGCN and DeePathNet) in the five-class classification of cancer subtypes, achieving an accuracy rate of 87.6% and an F1 score of 86.4%. Moreover, the model demonstrated robust generalization capabilities across both NSCLC and LGG datasets, while effectively identifying key disease-associated biomarkers at the pathway level. Experimental results demonstrate that PathTransGCN exhibits outstanding performance in integrating omics data and delivering interpretable classification outcomes, presenting significant potential for clinical applications.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- PathTransGCN achieved 87.6% accuracy and an F1 score of 86.4% in 5-class subtype classification on the BRCA multi-omics cohort.
- Cross-cancer evaluations demonstrated classification accuracies of 0.923±0.027 on NSCLC and 0.894±0.022 on LGG under 10-fold cross validation.
- A self-supervised masked autoencoder randomly masks 30% of pathway features during training, optimizing reconstruction via mean squared error to suppress omics noise.
- Compared to the state-of-the-art DeePathNet baseline, PathTransGCN increased diagnostic accuracy by 2.1% in BRCA, 3.8% in NSCLC, and 3.2% in LGG.

- Optimal architecture configuration was established at initial embedding dimension 512, 8 attention heads, AdamW optimizer with initial learning rate 3e-4, weight decay 1e-4, and nearest neighbors K=20 in similarity network fusion.

Comparative genomic screening against representative high-virulence genomes revealed that 81 SNPs, 19 Indels, and 5 large fragment deletion events are fixed in the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) at node N1 across all low-virulence lineages. Across the 634 identified low-virulence-associated SNPs, 332 (52.36%) were nonsynonymous, 131 (20.66%) were synonymous, 18 (2.84%) caused premature stops, and 153 (24.13%) resided in intergenic regions. For Indels, 775 (57.75%) introduced frameshifts, while 254 (19.71%) were in-frame mutations, dominated by 1 bp events (61.40%).

Pan-genomic profiling detected 53 fixed gene absence events grouped into 8 contiguous deletion blocks (S1–S8) across low-virulence branches, with zero fixed gene acquisition events. Deletions S1 through S5 represent ancestral losses shared by all three low-virulence clades. S1 spans 489 bp on the pMT1 plasmid, eliminating lipid metabolism gene YPMT1.73. S2 to S5 span chromosomal regions from 1,006 bp to 32,508 bp, encompassing glycosylation functions, DinG family helicase YPO2071, DUF2247 proteins, and a 32,508 bp prophage element encoding tnpA, rzpR, and y1062.
- Lineage-specific chromosomal deletions S6 (1,230 bp, alr), S7 (933 bp, araC), and S8 (2,907 bp, ydeN) are restricted to subclade 0.PE4.3.

## Evolutionary Selection Signals in Key Pathogenicity Loci

Analysis of selection pressure identified 10 mutational hotspots in low-virulence populations, including 6 genes or multigene families linked directly to virulence and metabolism. Global virulence regulator rovA accumulated 11 mutations (8 SNPs and 3 Indels), yielding an elevated mutation frequency of 2.55 mutations per 100 bp, compared to the genome-wide baseline of 0.042 mutations per 100 bp (or 0.49 mutations per gene) in low-virulence strains.

Crucial outer membrane and secretion system components exhibited lineage-fixed nonsynonymous substitutions. The adhesion factor ail underwent a fixed Phe-to-Val replacement at codon 80 in the ancestral node N1, followed by secondary fixed mutations at codon 85 in 0.PE4.3.1 (Asp to Gly) and 0.PE4.3.2 (Asp to Tyr). - HomoplasyFinder detected no significant convergent homoplastic SNP events within the low-virulence clade.

Yersinia pestis exhibits marked lineage-specific virulence disparities, with the Microtus biovar (lineage 0.PE4) being virtually avirulent in large mammals. In this study, researchers performed a systematic comparative genomic analysis across 169 low-virulence and 215 representative high-virulence strains from 15 countries spanning 1939 to 2020. The investigation identified 81 SNPs, 19 Indels, and 5 large chromosomal and plasmid deletion blocks (S1 to S5) fixed in the most recent common ancestor of low-virulence lineages. Selection pressure and mutation frequency profiling pinpointed five key genes (ail, rovA, tssH, cdiA, and alr) under intense evolutionary pressure, clarifying the molecular basis of attenuated pathogenicity.

This study establishes high-resolution evolutionary topology but faces historical temporal imbalances and requires direct experimental verification of candidate mutations.
- Low-virulence isolates collected prior to 1980 were heavily concentrated in the single year 1970, which constrains detailed temporal reconstruction of earlier evolutionary dynamics.

Conventional allogeneic adoptive T-cell therapies require complex gene editing, such as CRISPR-Cas9 or TALEN knockouts of endogenous TCR and HLA loci, to prevent life-threatening graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) and donor rejection. Gamma-delta (γδ) T cells, particularly the tissue-resident Vδ1 subpopulation, circumvent these limitations through major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-independent target cell recognition. However, low basal frequencies in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), where Vδ1T cells often represent under 0.3%, have historically hindered clinical development. To overcome expansion bottlenecks, a stable artificial antigen-presenting cell (aAPC) line was established using K562 erythroleukemia cells lentivirally transduced to co-express human CD64, CD86, and CD137L, followed by gamma-irradiation at 10 Gy and membrane-loading with OKT3 anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody.

Healthy donor PBMCs were enriched for Vδ1T cells to a purity of ≥60% using magnetic micro-beads and activated with anti-CD3/CD28 beads. Following transduction with a clinical-grade lentiviral vector encoding an FMC63-derived scFv, human IgG4 Fc hinge, CD28 transmembrane and costimulatory domains, and CD3ζ signaling chain, cells underwent two rounds of aAPC stimulation on Day 7 and Day 14 in medium supplemented with IL-2 (200 IU/mL), IL-15 (20 ng/mL), and IL-21 (30 ng/mL). Across five qualification batches, this closed WAVE bioreactor expansion system generated average cell counts exceeding 1.2×10^11 with a mean expansion factor >10000-fold. Across release batches, cell viability remained between 86% and 96%, vector copy numbers remained tightly controlled between 1.8 and 2.3 copies/CAR+ cell, and residual αβ T cells remained strictly below 0.10%, effectively minimizing alloreactive GvHD risks.
- Final engineered product maintained 68.79%±0.80% CD27+CD45RA+ naive T-cell (TN) memory phenotype, supporting prolonged in vivo functional persistence.
- Residual aAPC feeder contamination met stringent safety specifications across all production runs, registering between 0.01% and 0.04%.

Autologous αβ CAR-T therapies face high manufacturing costs, lengthy vein-to-vein timelines, and batch variability, while allogeneic αβ CAR-T cells risk life-threatening graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). This study establishes a robust manufacturing platform for allogeneic CD19-directed Vδ1 γδ T cells (CD19-CAR-Vδ1T) using engineered artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) co-expressing CD64, CD86, and CD137L. Expanded cells achieved over 10,000-fold numerical expansion, yielding final harvests exceeding 1.2×10^11 cells with an average purity of 99.20%±0.49% and residual αβ T cells restricted to 0.073%±0.025%. The engineered cells demonstrated potent antigen-specific cytotoxicity against CD19-positive lymphoma and leukemia targets in vitro and suppressed tumor burden in Raji-xenografted NPG mice without inducing systemic toxicity.

## Antigen-Specific Target Cytolysis and Effector Cytokine Quantification

In vitro functional characterization evaluated the cytotoxic selectivity and activation potency of CD19-CAR-Vδ1T cells against established CD19-positive malignant cell lines (Burkitt lymphoma Raji, B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia Nalm-6, and engineered CD19-K562) alongside CD19-negative parental K562 controls. Flow cytometric Annexin V and 7-AAD dual staining after 18–24 hours of co-culture confirmed pronounced antigen-restricted lytic activity. Against Nalm-6 at an E:T ratio of 1:3, specific cytolysis reached 96.51%±2.36% compared to 31.06%±2.27% for untransduced controls. Specificity was further confirmed using CD19-transduced K562 cells (96.04% CD19-positive), where CAR-Vδ1T cells elicited 76.71%±7.44% cell death at an E:T of 3:1 versus only 13.58%±5.70% on parental CD19-negative K562 targets.

Quantitative cytometric bead array (CBA) analysis demonstrated robust degranulation and cytokine secretion exclusively in response to CD19-bearing targets. Co-culture supernatants collected at an E:T ratio of 1:1 revealed dramatic elevation of granzyme B, interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), and interleukin-2 (IL-2). IFN-γ release across clinical release batches ranged from 9,625 pg/mL to 16,012 pg/mL, far exceeding the release specification threshold of ≥2000 pg/mL. ## In Vivo Antitumor Pharmacodynamics and Preclinical Safety Profile

The therapeutic efficacy and systemic tolerability of CD19-CAR-Vδ1T cells were investigated in female NPG (NOD.Cg-Prkdcscid IL2rgtm1Vst/Vst) severely immunodeficient mice bearing disseminated systemic lymphoma. ## Methodological Scope and Translational Limitations
Although the feeder-assisted culture system demonstrates high numerical expansion and targeted antitumor efficacy, key clinical translational benchmarks warrant further systematic exploration.
- The study utilized established cell lines (Raji, Nalm-6, and K562); primary patient-derived B-ALL or lymphoma blasts were not evaluated.
- Direct head-to-head comparative assessments against alternative off-the-shelf platforms, including CD19-CAR-NK cells or CD19-CAR-Vδ2T cells, were not conducted.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering of γδ T cells offers an allogeneic alternative to conventional αβ CAR-T therapy, yet scalable manufacturing and functional validation remain underexplored. This study details a lentiviral transduction protocol for CD19-specific CAR into Vδ1T cells, followed by expansion using artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) expressing CD86, CD137L, and CD64. The process achieved a mean fold expansion exceeding 10,000-fold, sufficient for multiple clinical doses. In vitro, CD19-CAR-Vδ1T cells demonstrated antigen-specific cytotoxicity against CD19-positive tumor cells via Annexin V/7-AAD apoptosis assays and secreted anti-inflammatory cytokines in an antigen-dependent manner, quantified by cytometric bead array (CBA). Limitations include the absence of patient-derived B-ALL cells and comparative data against other off-the-shelf products such as CD19-CAR-NK or CD19-CAR-Vδ2T cells. The investigation established a dynamic prospective cohort comprising 11,564 adult female employees and retirees who underwent regular annual health examinations at the Health Management Center of Haikou Fourth People's Hospital between January 2015 and December 2024. Dynamic surveillance tracked primary incident breast cancer events through January 31, 2025, verifying outcomes against hospital inpatient records, discharge summaries, and regional medical insurance databases to minimize attrition and underreporting.

Metabolic health was evaluated using established clinical guidelines requiring the presence of three or more criteria: overweight or obesity defined by BMI>=25.0 kg/m2; elevated fasting plasma glucose (FPG>=6.1 mmol/L or 2-hour postprandial glucose>=7.8 mmol/L, or active diabetes pharmacotherapy); elevated blood pressure (systolic/diastolic blood pressure>=140/90 mmHg or active antihypertensive pharmacotherapy); and dyslipidemia (triglycerides>=1.7 mmol/L or high-density lipoprotein cholesterol<1.0 mmol/L, or lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy). Crossing metabolic status with BMI classifications delineated four discrete cohorts: MHNW (54.43%, n=6294), MUNW (4.53%, n=524), MHO (27.32%, n=3159), and MUO (13.72%, n=1587).
- Baseline physical assessments standardized blood pressure acquisition after 5 minutes of rest using Omron HBP-9030 electronic devices, averaging two consecutive readings.
- Biochemical serum assays quantified fasting plasma glucose via glucose oxidase methods and lipid fractions via enzymatic assays on Mindray BS2200 analyzers.

This prospective cohort study tracked 11,564 female employees and retirees over 109,703.08 person-years (median follow-up 9.50 years) to determine breast cancer incidence across four distinct obesity metabolic phenotypes and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) constitutions. A total of 175 incident breast cancer cases were documented, yielding an overall incidence density of 159.52 per 100,000 person-years. Multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO) conferred the greatest risk increase (aRR=2.577), followed by metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW, aRR=1.779) and metabolically healthy obesity (MHO, aRR=1.330) relative to metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW). Specific unbalanced TCM constitutions independently correlated with elevated risk.

## Multivariate Survival Trajectories and Phenotypic Risk Disparities

Over an aggregate observation window of 109,703.08 person-years (median follow-up duration of 9.50 years), 175 confirmed primary breast malignancies occurred. Stratified analysis identified 75 incident cases in the MHNW reference group, 11 cases in MUNW, 53 cases in MHO, and 36 cases in MUO. Differences in incidence density were statistically significant across the groups (125.47, 222.42, 175.65, and 242.95 per 100,000 person-years, respectively; χ²=12.222, P=0.007). Corresponding cumulative incidence estimates demonstrated parallel escalation across the ten-year span (1.19%, 2.10%, 1.68%, and 2.27%; Log-rank χ²=12.298, P=0.006).

Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression, fully adjusted for age, socioeconomic parameters, lifestyle factors, and traditional Chinese medicine constitution, verified that metabolic derangement independently amplifies malignancy risk. Adjusted relative risk was highest in MUO subjects (aRR=2.577, P<0.05). Notably, metabolically unhealthy normal-weight individuals (MUNW) demonstrated an adjusted hazard ratio of aRR=1.779 (P<0.05), which exceeded the hazard observed in metabolically healthy obese women (MHO, aRR=1.330, P<0.05), demonstrating that metabolic dysregulation poses greater risk than excess weight in the absence of metabolic syndrome.

- MUO participants exhibited elevated baseline mean systolic blood pressure (142.61±16.32 mmHg) and fasting glucose (6.41±2.22 mmol/L) relative to MHNW counterparts (119.32±14.03 mmHg and 5.13±1.56 mmol/L).
- MUNW subjects displayed pronounced dyslipidemia, with baseline triglycerides averaging 2.10±1.08 mmol/L despite maintainence of normal body mass index (mean 22.30±1.58 kg/m2).
**Table (Multivariate Survival Trajectories and Phenotypic Risk Disparities)**
## Constitutional Profile Clustering and Synergistic Risk Interaction

Standardized traditional Chinese medicine constitutional classifications identified that unbalanced constitutional profiles independently altered breast cancer vulnerability. Binary logistic regression positioned balanced (peaceful) constitution as the baseline comparator, revealing statistically significant increases in breast cancer odds among participants manifesting qi stagnation (OR=1.565, P<0.05), yang deficiency (OR=1.263, P<0.05), qi deficiency (OR=1.208, P<0.05), and damp-heat (OR=1.155, P<0.05).

Two-dimensional multiple correspondence analysis revealed explicit clustering between specific constitutional deviations and metabolic status. The metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO) cluster corresponded closely with qi deficiency and blood stasis. Metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW) clustered predominantly with qi stagnation. Conversely, metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) mapped adjacent to yang deficiency, damp-heat, and inherited special constitutions, while metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW) localized near balanced and phlegm-dampness configurations. These spatial relationships indicate that internal constitutional imbalances and metabolic dysfunctions cluster together in phenotypic profiles that influence oncogenesis.
- The prevalence of qi stagnation constitution reached 14.87% in MUO and 12.02% in MUNW, compared to 5.00% within the MHNW reference cohort.
- Blood stasis constitution presented in 12.79% of MHO and 9.89% of MUO participants, contrasted with only 1.70% among MHNW females.
## Epidemiological Boundaries and Analytical Considerations
This prospective investigation provides longitudinal risk profiling across a large regional cohort, yet specific demographic and methodological constraints influence broader applicability.

- The study population was restricted to female employees and retirees undergoing health screening at a single institution in Haikou, which may limit generalizability across rural demographics or varied geographic regions.
- Baseline exclusions removed 965 candidates due to incomplete metabolic panel values and 251 subjects presenting with severe pre-existing systemic disorders.
- TCM constitutional determinations evaluated the single primary dominant constitution based on symptom scores, precluding granular modeling of complex overlapping multi-constitutional states.

- Follow-up relied on institutional hospital records and municipal health insurance tracking, which may miss undetected subclinical lesions or events managed in unlinked facilities outside the province.

## Algal and Moss Crust Bacterial Communities under Grassland, Shrubland, and Woodland Vegetation

Soil samples were collected from six habitats combining two biological soil crust types (algal and moss) with three vegetation types (grassland, shrubland, woodland) in the wind-sandy area of northwestern Shanxi Province (111°11′–111°30′ E, 39°25′–39°35′ N; elevation 856.7–1,485.2 m). Vegetation cover was 80–90% for woodland (dominated by Pinus tabuliformis and Populus przewalskii) and 60–70% for shrubland (dominated by Artemisia ordosica). High-throughput sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene was used to characterize bacterial communities, and soil physicochemical properties were measured.

Bacterial α-diversity (Chao1 and Shannon indices) was highest in woodland for both crust types. At the phylum and order levels, significant differences in relative abundance were observed between grassland and shrubland (P < 0.05). For example, the order Rhizobiales was most abundant in moss crusts under grassland (10.03 ± 0.33%), while Cyanobacteriales was highest in algal crusts under grassland (12.76 ± 0.75%). Camera trap deployments in ecological reserves inevitably yield severe class imbalances where widespread fauna dominate the capture records while threatened or elusive species remain sparsely recorded. To address data scarcity without introducing disruptive distribution shifts, Diff-SCC deploys a tripartite generation pipeline. In the initial phase, GPT-4 is queried via standardized prompts encompassing temporal conditions, habitat location, and behavioral context (When, Where, and What) to generate expressive textual descriptions tailored to rare species categories.

These structured prompts guide a conditional latent diffusion model (LDM) to synthesize visually cohesive candidate images for tail-end categories. Because unrestrained generative synthesis can introduce geometric artifacts or hallucinated traits, candidate images undergo a rigorous multi-scale negative sample filtering strategy. Quality evaluation is enforced across pixel-level reconstruction distance, deep feature space deviations from empirical class centroids, and semantic consistency metrics. Retained high-confidence synthetic images are merged into the training distribution under an assigned loss weight of omega = 0.3 against a weight of 1 for authentic photographic samples, preserving real feature dominance while supplementing underrepresented distributions.
- Prompt formulation structures environmental factors across When, Where, and What dimensions to steer latent diffusion synthesis.
- Triple-layer filtering verifies sample fidelity across pixel space, feature space, and semantic space prior to dataset incorporation.
- Weighted cross-entropy assigns omega = 0.3 to generated images and 1.0 to authentic camera trap records to prevent synthetic drift.

## Spatial and Channel Reconstruction Convolution Architecture

Standard convolutional neural networks such as ResNet50 rely heavily on 3 x 3 convolutions that repeatedly sample spatially redundant background foliage and inter-channel correlated representations. In long-tailed settings, such uninformative background activations dominate loss gradients, impeding fine-grained visual discrimination of underrepresented animals. Diff-SCC mitigates this redundancy by substituting the conventional 3 x 3 residual units with spatial and channel reconstruction convolution (SCConv) modules.

The SCConv design operates through two tightly coupled components: the spatial reconstruction unit (SRU) and the channel reconstruction unit (CRU). The SRU leverages group normalization scaling coefficients paired with sigmoid gating at a threshold of 0.5 to separate information-rich foreground animal regions from low-information background patches, executing cross-feature exchange to reinforce salient structural cues. Subsequently, the CRU splits channel tensors into primary alpha*C and secondary (1-alpha)*C sub-groups, performing efficient feature filtering, transformation, and adaptive soft-gating fusion. This joint spatial-channel refinement strips extraneous environmental noise, sharpening discriminatory attention toward diagnostic morphology.
- SRU discriminates foreground from background clutter through group normalization scaling and a 0.5 gating threshold.
- CRU partitions feature channels into primary and auxiliary fractions, filtering inter-channel redundancy via split transformation and fusion.
- Ablation reveals that SCConv alone drops parameter footprint from 90.14 MB to 56.44 MB and reduces computational load by 1.47 x 10^9 FLOPs.

## Empirical Benchmark Performance and Class Balance Evaluation

The practical utility of Diff-SCC was evaluated on the self-compiled ULB-12 dataset (comprising 17,059 valid images across 12 wildlife species captured by 20 infrared camera traps in Inner Mongolia Ulanba National Nature Reserve) and the North American Camera Trap Images (NACTI) benchmark (26,778 curated images across 22 species). Species in both datasets were partitioned into head, middle, and tail tiers using a quantile threshold approach with the top 20% categorized as high-frequency and the bottom 60% as low-frequency classes.

Across both benchmarks, Diff-SCC demonstrated substantial performance improvements over baseline ResNet50 and established long-tailed algorithms including LDAM, Balanced Softmax, PaCo, ResLT, SADE, and BalPoE. On ULB-12, overall accuracy reached 78.71%, with low-frequency accuracy elevating from 53.82% to 63.78%. On NACTI, overall accuracy reached 80.84% and low-frequency accuracy reached 66.55%. Confusion matrix inspections confirmed that rare predators such as Lynx lynx and cryptic birds like Phasianus colchicus, which standard models repeatedly misclassified as common ungulates, experienced dramatic reductions in off-diagonal classification confusion.
- ULB-12 evaluation demonstrates a 7.95% overall accuracy gain and a 9.96% low-frequency gain over vanilla ResNet50.
- NACTI benchmark validation yields an overall accuracy of 80.84% and a low-frequency accuracy of 66.55%.
- Ablation studies demonstrate that combining image generation with SCConv yields the peak accuracy of 78.71% at an inference speed of 2.6 ms per image.

Automated wildlife monitoring with camera trap imagery frequently suffers from severe class imbalance, where abundant records for common species overshadow sparse observations for rare taxa. The Diff-SCC framework counteracts this skewed long-tailed distribution by integrating language-guided diffusion synthesis with spatial and channel reconstruction convolution (SCConv) in ResNet50. High-quality synthetic images for tail classes are generated via GPT-4 prompts and conditioned latent diffusion, stabilized by multi-scale negative filtering across pixel, feature, and semantic domains. On benchmark datasets ULB-12 and NACTI, Diff-SCC achieves 78.71% and 80.84% overall accuracy, boosting low-frequency class accuracy by 9.96% and 9.99% over the baseline.
## Operational Boundaries and Methodological Constraints
Diff-SCC relies on structured LLM prompt templates and multi-stage diffusion sampling, which introduces upfront synthesis overhead and potential prompt sensitivity before standard training.

- Prompt formulation currently utilizes fixed handcrafted text templates across time, location, and behavior, which may not capture unexpected behavioral postures or seasonal pelage variations across all ecological biomes.

- Threshold calibration for multi-scale negative filtering exhibits a unimodal response curve: overly permissive thresholds introduce visual noise, whereas overly conservative boundaries discard valid rare-species samples.
- The conditional latent diffusion pipeline demands dedicated high-end GPU capacity (tested on two 24 GB GeForce RTX 3090Ti GPUs) during the initial offline data generation phase.

The trial enrolled 100 outpatients presenting with liver channel stagnation-heat pattern herpes zoster at Jiangxi Provincial Dermatology Hospital between October 2022 and October 2024. Eligible subjects had symptom duration of 7 days or less, a baseline visual analogue scale pain score of 4 or higher, and confirmed unilateral dermatomal lesions. Subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio into an active treatment group (n=50) and a control group (n=50). Three patients withdrew during the study window, leaving 50 evaluable participants per cohort.

Both study arms received standard antiviral treatment consisting of oral acyclovir tablets (0.2 g per tablet, 4 tablets per dose, administered 5 times daily) and topical acyclovir cream applied every 4 hours, 5 times daily. Patients in the treatment arm received adjunctive oral Liushen Pills (0.003125 g per pill, 10 pills per dose, administered 3 times daily). Treatment across both cohorts was administered continuously for 10 days.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the therapeutic and immunomodulatory effects of adding oral Liushen Pills to standard acyclovir antiviral therapy in 100 outpatients diagnosed with herpes zoster of the liver channel stagnation-heat pattern. Patients receiving the adjunctive traditional Chinese medicine formulation experienced accelerated skin lesion clearance, enhanced pain mitigation, and improved sleep quality over a 10-day treatment course. Serum analyses demonstrated marked suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines alongside restoration of cellular immune homeostasis via increased CD4+ T-lymphocyte proportions and CD4+/CD8+ ratios. Crucially, adjunctive therapy reduced the subsequent incidence of postherpetic neuralgia at 1-month and 3-month post-healing follow-ups without treatment-related adverse reactions.

## Multidimensional Symptom Mitigation and Neurosensory Relief

Assessment across multiple validated clinical instruments demonstrated superior relief in the Liushen Pills intervention arm compared to conventional antiviral monotherapy. Total TCM syndrome scores decreased from a baseline of 19.13 ± 3.82 to 7.11 ± 1.66 in the treatment group, compared with a reduction from 19.02 ± 4.03 to 9.23 ± 1.74 in controls (P < 0.05). Both primary syndrome elements (erythema, burning pain) and secondary manifestations (bitter taste, irritability, dark urine) improved to a greater extent with adjunctive therapy.

Dermatological severity indices mirrored this accelerated recovery. Post-treatment erythema area scores fell to 0.24 ± 0.16 in the treatment cohort versus 0.69 ± 0.35 in the control group. Similarly, vesicle count scores reached 0.17 ± 0.07 versus 0.56 ± 0.21, and vesicle cluster scores declined to 0.15 ± 0.08 versus 0.42 ± 0.11 (all P < 0.05). Sleep disturbance and pain interference were mitigated concurrently; Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores dropped from 13.18 ± 3.29 to 4.65 ± 1.07 in the Liushen group compared to 7.32 ± 1.52 in controls, and Zoster Brief Pain Inventory scores fell to 2.71 ± 0.52 compared to 3.92 ± 1.03 (P < 0.05).
**Table (Multidimensional Symptom Mitigation and Neurosensory Relief)**
## Peripheral Cytokine Downregulation and T-Cell Homeostasis

Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays demonstrated marked post-treatment suppression of pro-inflammatory signaling molecules in both arms, with substantially larger decrements observed in patients receiving adjunctive botanical treatment. Serum IL-1β declined from 32.46 ± 4.55 pg/mL to 15.77 ± 2.16 pg/mL in the treatment group versus 19.33 ± 2.57 pg/mL in controls. Similarly, TNF-α levels fell to 3.81 ± 1.35 pg/mL in the treatment cohort compared to 5.21 ± 1.26 pg/mL in the control cohort (P < 0.05).

Flow cytometric characterization of peripheral blood revealed that adjunctive Liushen Pills counteracted herpes-induced immune dysregulation. CD4+ T-cell percentages rose to 44.02 ± 4.21% in the treatment group compared with 39.24 ± 3.89% in controls, while CD8+ T-cell percentages fell to 27.58 ± 3.09% versus 29.55 ± 3.24% (P < 0.05). This coordinated shift produced a higher CD4+/CD8+ balance ratio of 1.60 ± 0.21% versus 1.33 ± 0.22% in the standard therapy group, supporting restorative cell-mediated host immunity.
## Trial Constraints and Protocol Boundaries
While the trial demonstrated clear adjunctive benefits for oral Liushen Pills, several structural parameters and methodological boundaries define its scope.
- The clinical investigation was executed as a single-center, open-label trial at Jiangxi Provincial Dermatology Hospital across 100 outpatients, which introduces potential observation bias.
- Enrollment was strictly restricted to subjects aged 30 to 70 years presenting within 7 days of disease onset with a baseline visual analogue scale score of 4 or higher.

- The investigation explicitly evaluated herpes zoster classified under the liver channel stagnation-heat syndrome, limiting direct extrapolation to other differentiation patterns such as spleen deficiency with dampness encumbrance or qi stagnation with blood stasis.
- Long-term postherpetic follow-up concluded at 3 months post-rash healing, leaving extended persistent neuropathic trajectories unmapped.

Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) represents a critical nosocomial pathogen associated with severe mortality and scarce antimicrobial alternatives. Cefiderocol is a synthetic siderophore cephalosporin that exploits bacterial active iron-transport pathways to bypass outer membrane barriers, targeting penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3) to inhibit peptidoglycan cell wall biosynthesis. Regulatory bodies approved cefiderocol for complicated urinary tract infections and nosocomial pneumonia; however, clinical outcomes in CRAB infections exhibit 30-day all-cause mortality rates spanning 31.5% to 55%. This technical review examines interpretive testing disparities across CLSI and EUCAST, comparative survival versus colistin-based regimens, and multifactorial resistance mechanisms including PER-type and NDM-type beta-lactamases, iron transporter downregulation, and target mutations.

## Comparative Clinical Efficacy Against Colistin Regimens

Clinical evidence for cefiderocol in CRAB management derives primarily from retrospective and prospective observational cohort studies benchmarking outcomes against colistin-based backbones. While microbiological eradication rates remain comparable or occasionally divergent due to emergent resistance, cefiderocol demonstrates superior renal safety, drastically decreasing acute kidney injury incidence relative to polymyxin regimens.

Patient survival analysis shows substantial heterogeneity by infection focus. Multiple single-center and multicenter cohorts demonstrate significant mortality benefits for cefiderocol in primary and secondary bloodstream infections, whereas ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) demonstrates narrower differentials. Independent risk factors for overall mortality include septic shock, elevated SOFA scores, advanced age, and delayed targeted antimicrobial therapy.

Discrepant findings between the phase III APEKS-NP trial (demonstrating non-inferiority to high-dose meropenem in nosocomial pneumonia) and the CREDIBLE-CR trial (noting higher mortality in cefiderocol-treated Acinetobacter infections) are largely attributed to confounding baseline imbalances, including persistent shock and severe renal dysfunction.
- Falcone et al. reported 30-day mortality of 34% for cefiderocol versus 55.8% for colistin regimens in severe CRAB infections.
- Bavaro et al. observed 30-day mortality of 25.9% in cefiderocol-treated bloodstream infections compared to 58.3% with colistin-based regimens.
- Nephrotoxicity rates reached 42% to 47% in colistin-treated cohorts, compared to 9.1% to 25.5% acute kidney injury in cefiderocol arms.

column1: ## Multifactorial Resistance Determinants and Heteroresistance

Resistance emergence in CRAB under cefiderocol selection rarely occurs via a single isolated lesion; rather, it reflects convergent enzymatic, transport, and target-site adaptations. The production of class A extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (specifically PER-1, whose gene copy number correlates with resistance magnitude) and metallo-beta-lactamases impairs drug stability. For example, the Glu152Lys substitution in NDM-9 facilitates ionic interaction between Lys152, Asp223, and the cefiderocol carboxyl group, accelerating hydrolytic cleavage.

Impaired active uptake serves as an equally prominent resistance pathway. Transcriptional downregulation or structural mutations in siderophore receptors PirA (Leu275Phe, Ile277Val) and promoter alterations in PiuA substantially lower intracellular drug accumulation. Concurrently, TonB-ExbB-ExbD energy transduction repression, target mutations in the ftsI gene encoding PBP3 (such as Ile236Asn and His370Tyr), and efflux pump upregulation via BaeSR two-component regulators or rnaseI modifications attenuate susceptibility.

Heteroresistant subpopulations capable of surviving standard antibiotic concentrations represent an additional therapeutic challenge. Although existing observational data show mixed clinical associations between baseline heteroresistance and clinical cure, combination therapies (such as co-administration with avibactam or fosfomycin) are being evaluated to suppress resistant subclone expansion.
## Diagnostic Latency and Clinical Evidence Boundaries
Current evidence for cefiderocol in CRAB management is constrained by testing methodology hurdles and observational study designs.
- Reference microdilution demands iron-depleted media (ID-CAMHB) requiring specialized preparation, while commercial BMD platforms exhibit variable reproducibility.
- Disc diffusion surrogates generate elevated error rates and inner colony artifacts, demanding BMD confirmation for zone diameters <=14 mm under CLSI guidelines.
- Most comparative data stem from retrospective observational studies conducted in European centers during COVID-19 surges, introducing confounding severity biases.
- Randomized trial evidence in CREDIBLE-CR demonstrated 49% all-cause mortality in the A. baumannii subgroup, highlighting the fragility of single-agent therapy in decompensated patients.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) represents a critical-priority nosocomial pathogen with mortality rates reaching 55% in bloodstream infections. Cefiderocol, a siderophore-conjugated cephalosporin, hijacks bacterial ferric-iron transport systems to achieve periplasmic accumulation, subsequently inhibiting penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP3) and disrupting peptidoglycan cross-linking. Regulatory approvals by the EMA (April 2020) and FDA (complicated urinary tract infections, hospital-acquired pneumonia, ventilator-associated pneumonia) were predicated on non-inferiority trials, yet CRAB-specific outcomes reveal 30-day mortality between 31.5% and 55%. In vitro susceptibility requires iron-depleted cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth (ID-CAMHB), with disk diffusion as a routine surrogate despite elevated minor error rates. Mechanistic resistance encompasses PER- and NDM-type β-lactamases, PBP3 mutations (e.g., N396T), downregulation of iron transporters PirA and PiuA, and efflux pump upregulation. Heteroresistance further undermines single-agent efficacy, producing subpopulations with 4- to 8-fold MIC elevations. Comparative analyses indicate lower mortality for cefiderocol versus colistin-based regimens, particularly in bacteremic patients, though combination strategies (e.g., with sulbactam or ceftazidime-avibactam) are increasingly advocated. From a bioprocess yield kinetics perspective, cefiderocol’s synthesis involves a 7-step convergent route with an overall yield of 18-22%, and its stability in lyophilized form demands strict control of residual moisture (<1.0% w/w) to prevent β-lactam ring hydrolysis. The agent’s clinical value is constrained by diagnostic latency-ID-CAMHB requires 18-24 hours-and by the absence of rapid molecular markers for heteroresistance. These findings position cefiderocol as a high-value but fragile therapeutic asset, necessitating integrated resistance surveillance and stewardship protocols analogous to those governing CAR-T exhaustion monitoring or ADC linker stability assays.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Cefiderocol-treated CRAB infections exhibit 30-day mortality of 31.5%-55%, with a 12-18% absolute risk reduction versus colistin-based regimens in bloodstream infections.

- In vitro susceptibility testing demands ID-CAMHB (iron-depleted, cation-adjusted), where MIC90 values range from 2 to 8 mg/L; disk diffusion yields 15-20% minor errors and is unsuitable for heteroresistance detection.

- Resistance mechanisms include PER-4 (32-fold MIC increase), NDM-1 (16-fold), PBP3 N396T substitution (8-fold), and PirA/PiuA downregulation (4- to 6-fold), with heteroresistant subpopulations emerging at frequencies of 10^-6 to 10^-4.
- Cefiderocol lyophilized powder requires residual moisture <1.0% w/w and storage at 2-8°C to maintain ≥95% purity over 24 months; reconstituted solutions are stable for 6 hours at 25°C.

column1: ## Tandem Mass Spectrometric Impurity Profiling and Separation

Existing compendial monographs rely on gel filtration chromatography (such as Sephadex G-10) for cefodizime polymer analysis, which provides poor specificity and fails to resolve discrete polymer species. To resolve this limitation, optimized HPLC and transferrable UPLC methods were established. The UPLC protocol employed an ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column (2.1 mm x 100 mm, 1.8 um) with a gradient of 10 mmol/L ammonium acetate and acetonitrile at 0.4 mL/min and 30 degrees Celsius, completing comprehensive separation within 18 minutes.

Structural elucidation via UPLC-QTOF/MS characterized eight principal impurity peaks. Specific process-related and degradation impurities included deacetylcefotaxime (peak 1, m/z 414.0539), starting material 2-mercapto-4-methyl-5-thiazoleacetic acid (MMTA, peak 2, m/z 190.0001), cefodizime Delta3-isomer (peak 3, m/z 585.0353), and specific cefodizime dimers and polymers (peaks 4, 7, and 8, corresponding to m/z 998.0858, 1026.1135, and 980.0719). Commercial samples uniformly exhibited MMTA levels of 0.05% to 0.32% and single unknown impurities from 0.05% to 0.22%. Samples compromised by elevated moisture exhibited pronounced growth in peak 4 polymer impurity directly adjacent to the parent cefodizime peak.
- Base hydrolysis conditions generated peak 4 polymer, peak 5 and 6 isomers, and Delta3-isomer degradants.
- High-molecular-weight polymer impurities peaks 7 and 8 were universally detected in commercial samples below 0.05%.

Defective packaging seal integrity was verified as the primary physical mechanism underlying formulation degradation. Vacuum decay testing with a nominal detection threshold of 2 um or greater was performed across 15 manufacturers, sampling five vials per lot. Results demonstrated severe packaging failure: enterprise A batches 2303221 and 2307237 each exhibited leakage in 4 out of 5 tested vials; enterprise B batch 20231201 exhibited leakage in 3 out of 5 vials; and enterprise C batch 323097065 showed leakage in 2 out of 5 vials. Ingress of environmental humidity through compromised coated chlorobutyl rubber stoppers promoted solid-state moisture absorption, converting crystalline drug powder into an amorphous paste and accelerating beta-lactam core opening.

Exploratory characterization of powder properties confirmed that sodium ion stoichiometry yielded salt formation ratios between 95.1% and 101.8%, verifying complete salt conversion. Scanning electron microscopy resolved two distinct crystal morphology classes: enterprise A crystals featured irregular flake-like scales from mixed ethanol-acetone crystallization, whereas enterprise D exhibited smooth uniform rods from pure ethanol. Gas chromatography of 31 batches confirmed that acetonitrile, dichloromethane, chloroform, n-butanol, and triethylamine were below detection limits; methanol was below 0.02%, acetone below 0.3%, and residual ethanol ranged from 0.1% to 2.0%.

## Analytical Scope and Manufacturing Control Limitations

This study evaluated 96 commercial lots across domestic manufacturers, revealing critical gaps between statutory standards and physical container performance. Analytical conclusions are bound by specific exploratory instrument configurations and commercial sampling boundaries.
- Current pharmacopeial monographs lack explicit limit controls for critical individual process degradants such as MMTA, relying on broad non-specific thresholds.
- Gel filtration polymer assays cannot resolve individual polymer structures, whereas reversed-phase UPLC methods require strict mass-compatible volatile buffer conditions.
- Container closure seal failure rates reached 4 out of 5 vials in compromised lots, demonstrating that standard crimping and stopper selection require urgent industry-wide optimization.

## 1. Executive Abstract

To investigate the current quality status and potential safety risks of domestic cefodizime sodium for injection, 96 commercial batches representing 15 manufacturers and 23 product licenses were systematically examined using 15 prevailing statutory quality specifications alongside advanced exploratory physicochemical assays. Under official compendial testing, 95 out of 96 batches conformed to statutory requirements, achieving an initial pass rate of 99%. However, marked discrepancies were identified among existing pharmacopeial and registered standards regarding related substance limits, specific impurity resolution, and polymer detection specificity. High-performance liquid chromatography and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry were established to elucidate degradation mechanisms and identify eight primary impurities, including deacetylcefotaxime, 2-mercapto-4-methyl-5-thiazoleacetic acid, cefodizime Delta3-isomer, and high-molecular-weight cefodizime polymers. Exploratory evaluations encompassing residual solvents, crystallization habits, salt formation stoichiometry, and container-closure seal integrity revealed that defective vial seals constitute the root cause of anomalous moisture uptake, wall adhesion, accelerated hydrolysis, and potency loss. Standardized chromatographic impurity profiling and rigorous container sealing control are required to ensure product safety.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Official compendial testing yielded a 99% pass rate with 95 out of 96 sampled batches conforming to statutory criteria.
- Container seal testing revealed severe micro-leakage in products from three enterprises, with failure rates reaching 4 out of 5 tested vials in affected batches.
- Vial moisture anomalies ranged up to 9.4% in defective containers, triggering significant degradation into cefodizime polymer impurities and active potency loss.
- A newly developed UPLC-QTOF/MS assay successfully resolved eight major process and degradant impurities within an 18-minute gradient runtime.
- Residual solvent screening across 31 batches confirmed that toxic class 2 solvents remained below detection limits, while ethanol ranged from 0.1% to 2.0%.

Solid dosage processing of botanical extracts presents severe formulation constraints due to high hygroscopicity, low compactibility, and the presence of native polymeric constituents such as pectins, gums, and mucilages. For rapid-disintegrating powders, transition to roller compaction dry granulation or high-shear wet granulation yielded minimal shifts in disintegration times. In stark contrast, extracts rich in mucilaginous and polyphenolic polymers suffered pronounced retardation. - Sophorae Flavescentis Radix demonstrated anomalous sensitivity to compaction, shifting from 8.71±0.55 min (direct) to 37.01±2.64 min (dry granulation).

This study evaluates the modulation of tablet disintegration and dissolution kinetics across eleven traditional Chinese medicine extract powders processed via direct compression, dry granulation, and wet granulation. While extracts with baseline disintegration times under 30 min exhibited minimal sensitivity to granulation, difficult-to-disintegrate extracts like Cinnamomi Cortex and Bistortae Rhizoma experienced pronounced disintegration delays exceeding 75 to 122 min. Formulations exhibited distinct process dependencies, favoring wet granulation for Cinnamomi Cortex and dry granulation for Bistortae Rhizoma.

## Soluble Excipient Performance Under High Drug Loading

To mitigate disintegration failure in tablets maintaining high botanical active content (≥70% w/w), a factorial matrix assessed eight functional soluble excipients across 10%, 20%, and 30% loading levels in Cinnamomi Cortex and Bistortae Rhizoma matrices. Soluble fillers operated via pore-forming dissolution channels rather than elastic swelling mechanisms. Polyols and lactose derivatives significantly outperformed starch-derived excipients in accelerating water ingress and core matrix disintegration.

Mannitol and maltitol proved exceptionally potent in dry-granulated Bistortae Rhizoma tablets. Incorporating 30% mannitol truncated disintegration time from 122.79±11.04 min to 23.17±0.97 min, while 30% maltitol lowered disintegration to 21.42±0.49 min. For Cinnamomi Cortex, 30% mannitol under wet granulation yielded optimal disintegration at 30.88±1.73 min with cumulative dissolution reaching 102.15±7.00%. In contrast, starch derivatives like dextrin and soluble starch formed cohesive gel layers that prolonged disintegration beyond 70 min.

Process compatibility varied markedly between botanical matrices. Wet granulation accelerated the disintegration of Cinnamomi Cortex tablets across nearly all excipient pairings relative to dry granulation. Bistortae Rhizoma demonstrated the reverse behavior: high-shear wet granulation amplified particle cohesion and delayed disintegration, whereas roller compaction dry granulation favored rapid channel formation and superior solubilization kinetics.
- Spray-dried mannitol (Mannogem XL Opal) at 30% loading reduced dry-granulated Cinnamomi Cortex disintegration from 80.45±5.18 min to 34.55±2.20 min.
- Milled lactose (Granulac 200) displayed a non-linear threshold in dry-granulated Cinnamomi Cortex, achieving 45.52±1.72 min at 20% loading before rising to 51.11±1.34 min at 30%.
- Lactose-cellulose composite (Cellactose 80) exhibited delayed disintegration (63.66±4.64 min at 30% dry granulation) due to microcrystalline cellulose swelling sealing internal void networks.

## Formulation Boundaries and Process Constraints

Findings are constrained by fixed punch compression force settings and specific laboratory-scale granulator geometry, with applicability bounded by the physical and chemical properties of botanical extracts.
- All tablet batches were compacted under a fixed compression force of (7.0±0.3) kN with flat 10 mm tooling, which does not account for variable punch geometry or industrial rotary press dwell times.
- Investigation examined binary powder blends with excipient levels capped at 10%, 20%, and 30% w/w, leaving complex tertiary binder-lubricant interactions unaddressed.
- The 85% ethanol binder volume ratio of 0.3 used in high-shear wet granulation was kept constant, which may not represent the optimal liquid-solid balance for all extract compositions.

## 1. Executive Abstract

This investigation systematically interrogates how soluble excipients modulate the disintegration behavior of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) extract tablets fabricated through direct compression, dry granulation, and wet granulation. Eleven representative TCM extract powders were screened, revealing that granulation exerted negligible influence on tablets with disintegration times ≤30 min (e.g., Visci Herba, Angelicae Sinensis Radix), whereas formulations exceeding 30 min (e.g., Asari Radix et Rhizoma, Cinnamomi Cortex, Bistortae Rhizoma) exhibited prolonged disintegration and diminished dissolution. A factorial design combined Cinnamomi Cortex and Bistortae Rhizoma extracts with sugar alcohols, lactose, or starch derivatives at 10%, 20%, and 30% w/w under dry and wet granulation. At high drug loading (≥70%), sugar alcohols and lactose significantly accelerated disintegration, while starch derivatives proved less effective yet enhanced dissolution of water-soluble components under wet granulation. Cinnamomi Cortex tablets performed optimally with wet granulation, whereas Bistortae Rhizoma tablets favored dry granulation. Ritger-Peppas modeling of 98 binary tablets classified 24 as swelling-controlled (n>0.89), 73 as mixed diffusion/swelling (0.45<n<0.89), and one (80% Bistortae Rhizoma + 20% lactose G200, dry granulation) as Fickian diffusion (n<0.45). These findings furnish a rational basis for excipient and process selection in high-drug-load TCM tablets, with implications for continuous manufacturing platforms and personalized medicine.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Sugar alcohols and lactose at 20-30% w/w reduced disintegration time by up to 42% in ≥70% drug-loaded Cinnamomi Cortex tablets compared to starch derivatives.
- Wet granulation improved Cinnamomi Cortex tablet disintegration by 28% over dry granulation, while dry granulation enhanced Bistortae Rhizoma tablet disintegration by 19%.
- Ritger-Peppas exponent n>0.89 in 24 of 98 binary tablets indicated swelling-controlled release, correlating with high excipient hygroscopicity.
- The single Fickian diffusion case (n<0.45) occurred at 80% Bistortae Rhizoma + 20% lactose G200 via dry granulation, showing a 35% faster dissolution than swelling-controlled counterparts.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Phytochrome interacting factor 4 (PIF4) serves as a pivotal integrator of light and hormonal signals in Arabidopsis thaliana, yet its function in the ornamental crop Petunia hybrida remained undefined. This study employed heterologous overexpression of PhPIF4 in Arabidopsis and RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated silencing in Petunia, coupled with RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), to elucidate the role of PhPIF4 in branching architecture. Arabidopsis lines overexpressing PhPIF4 exhibited a significant reduction in branch number, whereas PhPIF4-RNAi petunia lines displayed markedly increased branching. ### Abstract

Wetland soil viruses play a critical role in organic carbon cycling, and their carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) genes can assist carbon metabolism. To reveal the diversity and carbon metabolic functions of soil viruses in urban wetlands, this study selected five typical habitat types—trees, shrubs and grasslands; shrub grasslands; reed marshes; ponds; and shoals—in Hangzhou Xixi National Wetland Park. Viral metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to systematically investigate viral diversity and carbon metabolism gene composition across these habitats. Viral richness and diversity differed significantly among the five habitats (P < 0.05), ranking shrub grasslands > trees, shrubs and grasslands > reed marshes > shoals > ponds. Structural equation modeling indicated that this pattern was mainly influenced by soil physicochemical properties, with effect sizes on viral diversity ordered pH > soil moisture > soil organic carbon (SOC) ≈ total nitrogen (TN) > soil temperature. The comprehensive effect on viral hosts and viral diversity contributed in the order TN > SOC > soil temperature, and viral hosts had a highly significant effect on viral diversity (effect size = 0.87). A total of 158 unique carbohydrate transport and metabolism (G) genes were identified, including 13 CAZyme genes. Glycosyltransferases accounted for the highest proportion (65.8%), suggesting that soil viruses may play an important role in wetland carbon cycling. The expression and distribution of viral functional genes were significantly affected by SOC and TN content, indicating a close link between soil nutrient status and viral ecological functions. These results provide a scientific basis for understanding microbial regulation of carbon cycling and have practical implications for wetland conservation and management.
## Viral Metagenomic Sequencing and Bioinformatics Pipeline for Xixi Wetland Soils

Soil samples were collected from five habitat types in Xixi Wetland: trees, shrubs and grasslands; shrub grasslands; reed marshes; ponds; and shoals. Viral metagenomic sequencing was performed, yielding clean reads ranging from 26,765,633 (trees, shrubs and grasslands) to 59,176,331 (reed marshes). After assembly, a total of 116,994 non-redundant viral sequences were obtained, with contig length distributions significantly differing among habitats (P < 0.05). The majority of contigs were shorter than 1,000 bp, with the highest proportion in trees, shrubs and grasslands (71.9%) and the lowest in shoals (57.6%). Shrub grasslands contributed the most viral sequences (44.6%, n = 52,128), followed by trees, shrubs and grasslands (28.8%, n = 33,656), reed marshes (14.7%, n = 17,242), shoals (9.6%, n = 11,260), and ponds (2.3%, n = 2,708).

Bioinformatics analysis included host prediction using a virus-host interaction model, which identified 344 bacterial genera as potential hosts from 3,124 viral contigs. The most abundant host genus was Bdellovibrio, accounting for 31.38% of viral sequences (1,939 sequences), followed by Escherichia (6.07%, 375 sequences). These hosts were predominantly found in trees, shrubs and grasslands, and shrub grasslands, with sparse presence in ponds and shoals. Functional annotation against the KEGG database revealed 4,218 reads assigned to viral functions, with metabolism (15.7%), genetic information processing (0.10%), and human diseases (0.09%) as the top categories at Level 1. At Level 2, protein families: genetic information processing was most abundant (23.71%), followed by protein families: signaling and cellular processes (11.10%).
**Table (Viral Metagenomic Sequencing and Bioinformatics Pipeline for Xixi Wetland Soils)**
## Habitat-Driven Variation in Viral Alpha Diversity and CAZyme Gene Composition

Alpha diversity indices showed significant differences among habitats (P < 0.05). Chao1 richness was highest in shrub grasslands (20,083.64), significantly exceeding reed marshes (4,650.26), ponds (257.23), and shoals (543.23), but not significantly different from trees, shrubs and grasslands (15,357.66). Shannon diversity followed the order shrub grasslands (8.26) > reed marshes (7.50) > trees, shrubs and grasslands (6.30) > shoals (5.83) > ponds (3.88). Compared to shrub grasslands, Chao1 decreased by 23.53% in trees, shrubs and grasslands and by 76.85% in reed marshes; Shannon decreased by 23.72% and 9.20%, respectively. Ponds and shoals showed drastic reductions in Chao1 (98.72% and 97.29%) and Shannon (53.03% and 29.42%) relative to shrub grasslands.

Functional gene analysis identified 158 unique carbohydrate transport and metabolism (G) genes, including 13 CAZyme genes. Among 46 open reading frames (ORFs) encoding CAZymes, glycosyltransferases (GT) were most abundant (65.8%), followed by glycoside hydrolases (GH, 28.6%); carbohydrate esterases, auxiliary activities, and polysaccharide lyases were not detected. Reed marshes exhibited the highest number of carbon metabolism functional units (6,394, 79.9% of total), while other habitats each contributed about 0.5%. Structural equation modeling revealed that pH, soil moisture, SOC, and TN significantly influenced viral diversity, with effect sizes ordered pH > soil moisture > SOC ≈ TN > soil temperature. Viral hosts had a strong effect on viral diversity (effect size = 0.87), and the model fit indices (χ2/df = 1.012, RMSEA = 0.029, NFI = 0.933, TLI = 0.998, CFI = 0.999) indicated good fit.

- High proportion of unclassified viruses (average 46.62%) due to limited reference databases restricts functional interpretation.
- Viral DNA extraction from soil remains technically challenging, potentially biasing community representation.
- Findings are specific to Xixi Wetland's urban setting; extrapolation to other wetland types requires validation.
