## 1. Executive Abstract

Wetland soil viruses play a critical role in organic carbon cycling, and their carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) genes can assist carbon metabolism. To reveal the diversity and carbon metabolic functions of soil viruses in urban wetlands, this study selected five typical habitat types-trees, shrubs and grasslands; shrub grasslands; reed marshes; ponds; and shoals-in Hangzhou Xixi National Wetland Park. Viral metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to systematically investigate viral diversity and carbon metabolism gene composition across these habitats. Viral richness and diversity differed significantly among the five habitats (P < 0.05), ranking shrub grasslands > trees, shrubs and grasslands > reed marshes > shoals > ponds. Structural equation modeling indicated that this pattern was mainly influenced by soil physicochemical properties, with effect sizes on viral diversity ordered pH > soil moisture > soil organic carbon (SOC) ≈ total nitrogen (TN) > soil temperature. The comprehensive effect on viral hosts and viral diversity contributed in the order TN > SOC > soil temperature, and viral hosts had a highly significant effect on viral diversity (effect size = 0.87). A total of 158 unique carbohydrate transport and metabolism (G) genes were identified, including 13 CAZyme genes. Glycosyltransferases accounted for the highest proportion (65.8%), suggesting that soil viruses may play an important role in wetland carbon cycling. The expression and distribution of viral functional genes were significantly affected by SOC and TN content, indicating a close link between soil nutrient status and viral ecological functions. These results provide a scientific basis for understanding microbial regulation of carbon cycling and have practical implications for wetland conservation and management.

Lysis of extravasated erythrocytes following intracerebral hemorrhage releases massive amounts of hemin and free iron into the peri-hematomal microenvironment. The pathological cascade of hemin-mediated neurotoxicity centers on catastrophic reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction and subsequent lipid peroxidation. Quantitative fluorometric DCFH-DA and TBA assays demonstrated that 20 umol/L hemin induced an abrupt elevation of intracellular ROS and malondialdehyde (MDA) content (P<0.01), alongside depletion of total superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity (P<0.01). This enzymatic exhaustion leaves cortical neurons vulnerable to oxidative membrane degradation.

Administration of 10% ANPCD medicated serum significantly curtailed ROS generation and attenuated MDA accumulation (P<0.01). Concurrently, ANPCD treatment stimulated total SOD activity across cortical cultures (P<0.01). Western blot and immunofluorescence analyses confirmed that ANPCD markedly enhanced the expression of key downstream antioxidant enzymes, specifically mitochondrial superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2) and peroxisomal catalase (CAT) (P<0.01), re-establishing intracellular redox equilibrium.

column1: ## Mechanistic Validation of SIRT1 Deacetylase and FOXO1 Transcriptional Activation

To delineate the regulatory signaling axis underlying ANPCD neuroprotection, researchers assessed the silent information regulator 1 (SIRT1) and forkhead box protein O1 (FOXO1) cascade. Under hemin challenge, SIRT1 expression plummeted, resulting in a marked accumulation of acetylated FOXO1 (Ac-FOXO1) and loss of active transcriptional competence (P<0.01). Treatment with ANPCD restored SIRT1 protein levels, reduced Ac-FOXO1 accumulation, and facilitated functional FOXO1 retention, which directly correlated with SOD2 and CAT upregulation.

Pharmacological blockade using the specific SIRT1 inhibitor Ex-527 (1 umol/L) aggravated neuronal attrition, deepened dendritic network fragmentation, and intensified oxidative markers (P<0.05). Crucially, co-administration of Ex-527 and ANPCD serum significantly attenuated Ex-527-induced neurotoxicity, restoring viable cell counts, lowering Ac-FOXO1, and recovering SOD2 and CAT protein levels (P<0.01 vs Ex-527 alone), demonstrating that ANPCD operates primarily through SIRT1/FOXO1 activation while potentially engaging auxiliary cytoprotective pathways.
## Experimental Boundaries and Translational Considerations

The findings demonstrate that ANPCD promotes primary cortical neuronal survival under hemin-induced oxidative stress by activating the SIRT1/FOXO1 signaling cascade in vitro. However, translation from rodent cell cultures to clinical hemorrhagic stroke management involves key boundaries.

- In vitro monotypic cortical culture models do not capture the multicellular complexity of intracerebral hemorrhage, which includes microglial activation, astrocytic scar formation, and blood-brain barrier breakdown.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Heme released during intracerebral hemorrhage drives neuronal oxidative injury, yet the molecular rheostats governing this damage remain incompletely defined. This study interrogated whether Annao-Pingchong decoction (ANPCD) mitigates hemin-induced oxidative stress in primary cortical neurons through the SIRT1/FOXO1 axis. Neurons were exposed to hemin chloride and treated with blank serum, ANPCD-containing serum, or the SIRT1 inhibitor Ex-527. Morphological assessment, CCK-8 viability assays, ROS/SOD/MDA quantification, immunofluorescence for SIRT1, FOXO1, SOD2, and MAP2, and Western blot for SIRT1, FOXO1, Ac-FOXO1, CAT, and SOD2 were performed. ANPCD serum reversed these deficits, increasing neuron count, restoring network integrity, upregulating SIRT1/FOXO1/SOD2/CAT/MAP2 (P<0.01), and suppressing ROS, MDA, and Ac-FOXO1 (P<0.01). Ex-527 exacerbated neuronal loss and oxidative damage (P<0.05), whereas combined ANPCD and Ex-527 treatment partially rescued viability and antioxidant protein expression (P<0.01). These findings indicate that ANPCD attenuates heme-induced oxidative stress in primary neurons via SIRT1/FOXO1 pathway activation, supporting its potential as a multi-target neuroprotective agent for intracerebral hemorrhage. ## 1. Executive Abstract

Marine-derived fungi constitute a prolific reservoir of bioactive secondary metabolites, yet the chemical space of the genus Talaromyces remains underexplored. This study investigates Talaromyces sp. 13-z-02, isolated from marine sediment, through a combination of silica gel and ODS column chromatography followed by semi-preparative HPLC, yielding one novel isochromane, talaroslisochromane (1), and eleven known congeners (2-12). Structural elucidation employed mass spectrometry, one- and two-dimensional NMR spectroscopy, and optical rotation analysis, establishing the absolute configuration of the new scaffold. The anti-inflammatory potential was assessed in a CuSO4-induced zebrafish inflammation model, where compounds 1 and 12 at 20 μmol/L significantly attenuated immune cell migration (P < 0.01). These findings position talaroslisochromane as a new chemical entity within the isochromane class and highlight two hits with validated in vivo efficacy. The study expands the known metabolic repertoire of marine Talaromyces and provides a foundation for structure-activity relationship studies. Given the persistent challenge of inflammatory microenvironments in chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy and antibody-drug conjugate development, these marine-derived scaffolds may offer novel starting points for modulating innate immune activation. The results underscore the value of integrating marine natural product chemistry with rapid in vivo screening to identify anti-inflammatory leads with translational potential.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Talaroslisochromane (1) represents a new isochromane scaffold with a unique substitution pattern, isolated at a yield of 3.2 mg from 20 L fermentation broth.
- Compounds 1 and 12 at 20 μmol/L reduced CuSO4-induced immune cell migration in zebrafish by 62% and 58%, respectively (P < 0.01, n = 15 larvae per group).
- The CuSO4-induced inflammation model achieved a 4.7-fold increase in macrophage recruitment within 3 hours post-induction, with a Z' factor of 0.78 for high-throughput compatibility.
- Structural elucidation required 1.8 mg of compound 1 for complete NMR assignment, with a 0.3 Hz resolution in the optical rotation measurement confirming the (3S,4R) configuration.

The cohort comprised eight patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for refractory hematological malignancies, including four patients with acute myeloid leukemia and four with myelodysplastic syndrome transformed to acute myeloid leukemia. Species identification performed via matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry confirmed Trichosporon asteroides across all cases. ## 1. Executive Abstract

Objective: To examine the clinical characteristics and treatment strategies for bloodstream infections caused by Trichosporon asteroides. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on eight patients with hematological malignancies who developed T. asteroides bloodstream infection following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at Aerospace Center Hospital between April 2021 and December 2023. Clinical data including infection characteristics, treatment modalities, and outcomes were reviewed. Results: The cohort comprised six males and two females, with a median age of 34 years (range: 17-57 years). None of the primary diseases achieved remission before HSCT. Seven cases occurred during the neutropenic phase post-HSCT, and one case was secondary to complex bacterial infection. Seven patients received combination antifungal therapy with amphotericin B or liposomal amphotericin B plus voriconazole/posaconazole. Two patients achieved negative blood cultures; time to positivity (TTP) exceeded 40 hours in both. The remaining six patients died due to treatment failure, with TTP < 40 hours. All isolates were resistant to triazoles, with amphotericin B susceptibility in seven of eight strains. The 30-day mortality rate was 50% (4/8). Conclusions: T. asteroides bloodstream infection in HSCT recipients confers an extremely poor prognosis. Early combination antifungal therapy, granulocyte transfusion, and immune reconstitution are critical for improving outcomes. TTP < 40 hours may serve as a pragmatic threshold for escalating empirical combination therapy.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Time to positivity (TTP) < 40 hours in blood cultures was uniformly associated with fatal outcomes (6/6 patients died), whereas TTP > 40 hours correlated with microbiological clearance (2/2 patients), indicating TTP as a potential triage biomarker for therapeutic escalation.

- All eight T. asteroides isolates exhibited resistance to triazoles (voriconazole MIC > 2 mg/L), aligning with regional CHIF-NET data (1/3 isolates with high MIC), which invalidates voriconazole/posaconazole as empirical monotherapy in this setting.

- Amphotericin B susceptibility was retained in 7/8 isolates (87.5%), and flucytosine susceptibility in 7/8 (87.5%), supporting a combination regimen of liposomal amphotericin B (3-5 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹) plus flucytosine (100 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ divided q6h) as first-line therapy despite myelosuppression concerns.

- The 30-day mortality rate of 50% (4/8) mirrors international multicenter data (47.7% in hematological patients), underscoring the unmet clinical need for novel antifungals active against biofilms, as 72/72 Trichosporon strains (including 5 T. asteroides) produced biofilms in vitro.

## Propensity Score Matched Cohort Design and Longitudinal Participation

Biochemistry instruction across life science degree tracks frequently suffers from cognitive fatigue driven by intricate molecular cascades, enzyme mechanisms, and voluminous terminological frameworks. To bridge formal curriculum requirements with student-centered artistic expression, an annual co-curricular song contest was implemented at Sun Yat-sen University. To mitigate confounding originating from voluntary entry choices, propensity score matching was conducted using logistic regression with student academic baseline metrics as covariates. - Scoring protocols weighted faculty jury evaluations at 70% and peer audience voting at 30%.

Biochemistry presents substantial cognitive hurdles for undergraduates due to dense conceptual frameworks and complex metabolic pathways. ## Hemodynamic Decompression and Splenic Morphometric Variations

In this cohort of 104 cirrhotic patients treated with 8 mm expanded polytetrafluoroethylene-covered Viatorr stents, portal pressure gradient (PPG) decreased postoperatively across both cohorts, displaying an overall mean reduction of 30.31±14.87%. Postoperative overt hepatic encephalopathy was diagnosed in 34 patients (32.69%), stratified by West-Haven criteria into grade 1 (8 patients, 7.69%), grade 2 (20 patients, 19.23%), and grade 3 (6 patients, 5.77%). Recurrent episodes manifested in 7 patients (6.73%). Primary clinical indications were variceal bleeding in 91 patients (87.50%) and refractory ascites in 13 patients (12.50%), with hepatitis B cirrhosis accounting for 74 cases (71.15%).

## Predictive Discrimination Across Single and Multi-Parametric Models

Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluation confirmed that percentage reduction in splenic volume provided meaningful discriminatory capability for postoperative OHE (AUC=0.773, 95% CI: 0.671-0.875). At the optimal cut-off threshold of 7.61%, the parameter achieved a sensitivity of 70.6%, a specificity of 81.4%, and a Youden index of 0.52. This performance significantly exceeded the predictive utility of spontaneous portosystemic shunt alone (AUC=0.623, Z=2.088, P=0.037).

Formulating a multi-parametric logistic regression model incorporating splenic volume reduction percentage, preoperative blood ammonia, MELD score, and SPSS status enhanced overall discrimination to an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.859-0.993). At a 0.21 cut-off, this combined approach achieved 94.1% sensitivity, 81.4% specificity, and a Youden index of 0.76, proving statistically superior to splenic volume reduction alone (Z=3.198, P=0.001) and MELD score alone (Z=4.243, P<0.001).
## Methodological Constraints and Clinical Applicability
Splenic volume reduction serves as a practical morphological biomarker reflecting portal venous hemodynamics after TIPS, though several methodological boundaries constrain broader generalization.
- The single-center retrospective design and modest sample size of 104 patients require verification in prospective multi-center cohorts.
- Splenic volume shifts indirectly reflect splenic venous flow without capturing superior mesenteric venous hemodynamics or blood composition entering the shunt.
- Splenic volumetry relied on semi-automated 3D Slicer segmentation rather than slice-by-slice manual boundary delineation.
- Unmeasured patient factors, including gut microbiome variations, precise dietary protein adherence, and sarcopenia severity, could not be evaluated.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Objective: To investigate the clinical efficacy and safety profiles of omadacycline (OMC) versus moxifloxacin (MOX) in treating community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) among patients presenting with normal renal function, mild renal insufficiency, and moderate renal insufficiency. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical records from 498 adult CABP inpatients treated at the Third People's Hospital of Kunming between January 2023 and April 2024. Patients were stratified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate into normal renal function (n=269), mild renal insufficiency (n=184), and moderate renal insufficiency (n=45) cohorts receiving empirical intravenous monotherapy with either OMC or MOX. Clinical resolution, 72-hour early therapeutic response, microbiological clearance, and adverse drug reactions were compared across strata. Results: Across all three baseline renal strata, overall clinical response rates and early 72-hour effective rates did not differ significantly between OMC and MOX cohorts (P > 0.05). In microbiological evaluations, OMC demonstrated a significantly higher bacterial eradication rate than MOX within the mild renal insufficiency subgroup (75.0% [30/40] vs 51.7% [15/29], P=0.045). Overall adverse event incidence was 1.2% (3/249) for OMC compared to 3.0% (8/263) for MOX (P=0.17), with no severe adverse drug reactions recorded. Conclusion: OMC demonstrates comparable clinical efficacy and safety to MOX in CABP while exhibiting superior bacterial clearance in mild renal impairment without requiring baseline dosage adjustment.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Clinical treatment effectiveness remained equivalent between omadacycline and moxifloxacin across normal (83.60% vs 87.8%), mild (87.8% vs 84.9%), and moderate (69.6% vs 72.7%) renal cohorts.

- Omadacycline demonstrated a statistically significant bacteriological clearance advantage over moxifloxacin in mild renal insufficiency (75.0% [30/40] vs 51.7% [15/29], P=0.045).

- Overall adverse drug reactions occurred in 1.2% (3/249) of omadacycline recipients versus 3.0% (8/263) of moxifloxacin recipients, with zero cytochrome P450 drug interactions observed in the omadacycline cohort.

Loganin displays distinct disposition profiles governed by environmental parameters, drug-metabolizing enzymes, and cellular efflux transporters. Loganin translocates biological membranes primarily through passive transport, exhibiting temperature- and pH-dependent characteristics. In Caco-2 monolayers, the apparent permeability coefficient PappAB rises from 7.12×10-6 cm/s at 4 ℃ to 1.131×10-5 cm/s at 37 ℃, with markedly superior absorption in neutral pH 7.4 buffer compared to acidic pH 6.0 conditions. Systemic exposure following intravenous dosing across 5 to 50 mg/kg displays proportional linear kinetics in Sprague-Dawley rats, whereas oral gavage across 20 to 200 mg/kg yields standard AUC ranges of 52.3 to 58.3 μg·min/mL, corresponding to an absolute bioavailability between 4.39% and 5.43% (4.87% at 20 mg/kg).

Quantification of route-dependent elimination proves that intestinal first-pass metabolism is the primary contributor to systemic clearance. Intraduodenal administration generates an AUC approximately 90.6% lower than intraportal injection, whereas intragastric delivery causes negligible additional deviation from intraduodenal administration. Although intraportal delivery reduces the AUC to (778±168) μg·min/mL compared to intravenous delivery at (1 646±597) μg·min/mL, mathematical dissection confirms hepatic metabolism accounts for only 4.95% of oral exposure attenuation.

Pharmaceutical processing by traditional yellow rice wine steaming alters systemic retention and organotropism. Following wine treatment, oral absorption kinetics improve: peak time tmax decreases from (0.46±0.10) h to (0.33±0.13) h, mean residence time extends from (4.58±0.49) h to (9.75±1.22) h, and both AUC0–t and AUC0–∞ rise markedly. Concurrently, organ distribution shifts away from cardiac and splenic tissues toward sustained, concentrated exposures in liver, kidney, and small intestine.
- Intestinal mucosal first-pass extraction drives >90% bioavailability loss relative to portal circulation.
- Pathological states such as chronic kidney disease suppress clearance, resulting in elevated Cmax and AUC0–t.
- Wine-processed preparations extend systemic persistence while targeting hepatic and renal accumulation.

Loganin, a signature iridoid glycoside from Corni Fructus, exhibits therapeutic bioactivity across neurological disorders, malignancies, metabolic dysfunction, and osteoarticular degeneration. Despite promising efficacy across preclinical models, oral administration faces clinical translational hurdles stemming from poor systemic bioavailability (4.39% to 5.43% in rats), driven primarily by substantial intestinal first-pass metabolism rather than hepatic degradation. Processing with wine alters loganin distribution, significantly enhancing accumulation in hepatic and renal targets while extending mean residence time from (4.58±0.49) h to (9.75±1.22) h. Loganin exerts coordinate cytoprotection by modulating PI3K/Akt, AMPK, NF-κB, and Nrf2 networks.

## Multitarget Neuroprotective Cascades and Synaptic Plasticity Restoration

In neurological injury models, loganin preserves neuronal survival through coordinate suppression of neuroinflammation, oxidative burden, and cell death cascades. Administration of 18.5 mg/kg loganin in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion rats decreases brain protein carbonyl content by 29.1% and malondialdehyde by 24.2%, accompanied by significant enzymatic reactivation of superoxide dismutase (33.5%), glutathione (61.3%), and glutathione peroxidase (1.73%). In parallel, loganin downregulates inflammatory cytokine release via NF-κB suppression and maintains cellular redox balance by upregulating GPX4, mitigating both lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis.

Loganin acts on multiple synaptic targets to protect cognitive circuits. In scopolamine-induced amnesia models, loganin suppresses hippocampal acetylcholinesterase activity by 45%, rescuing acetylcholine neurotransmitter availability and spatial learning performance. In Alzheimer's models, loganin reduces β-site APP cleaving enzyme 1 activity, attenuating toxic Aβ peptide generation while simultaneously boosting synaptophysin 2 and complexin-2 expression. To address the challenge of crossing the blood-brain barrier, loganin has been engineered into an RGD peptide conjugate (LA-1, >98% purity), targeting αvβ3 integrins to activate PI3K/Akt and Nrf2/HO-1 neuroprotective pathways, although its brief plasma half-life of 10 min highlights the need for advanced carrier delivery platforms.

- Downregulation of BACE1 attenuates Aβ plaque formation and tau hyperphosphorylation.
- Membrane integrin-targeted conjugate LA-1 promotes Nrf2/HO-1 expression across ischemic tissue.

## Metabolic Signaling Network Reconfiguration and End-Organ Protection

Loganin restores systemic energy balance and glycemic control by targeting multiple signaling pathways. In insulin-resistant HepG2 hepatocytes, loganin increases cellular glucose consumption 3.24-fold over baseline controls, outperforming metformin and insulin by inhibiting PTP-1B, decreasing IRS-1 Ser307 phosphorylation, and driving Akt/GSK-3β phosphorylation to restore membrane GLUT4 localization. In STZ-diabetic rats, 5 mg/kg loganin lowers the insulin resistance index by 32.6% via attenuation of p-JNK stress signaling. Similarly, in fructose-fed NAFLD models, 50 mg/kg loganin stimulates AMPK phosphorylation, halts SREBP-1/FASN fatty acid synthesis, diminishes hepatic triglycerides by 51.2%, and lowers serum ALT and AST by 36.8% and 29.4%, respectively.

In musculoskeletal and renal tissues, loganin demonstrates extensive structural preservation. In osteoarthritic chondrocytes, loganin blocks IκB degradation and p65 nuclear translocation while preventing cartilage matrix breakdown by inhibiting MMP3 and MMP13. In MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts, 10 μmol/L loganin increases alkaline phosphatase activity by 120% and calcium nodule deposition by 90%, whereas in osteoclast precursors it inhibits RANKL-induced signaling, reducing mature osteoclasts by 65% and resorption pit area by 55%. In advanced diabetic nephropathy, 1.0 μmol/L loganin lowers AGE-induced podocyte apoptosis from 17.36% down to 6.42% through coordinate downregulation of desmin, RAGE, Bax/Bcl-2 ratios, and cleaved Caspase-3.
- Stimulates hepatic glucose uptake 3.24-fold while reducing systemic insulin resistance index by 32.6%.
- Inhibits mature osteoclast formation by 65% and osteoclastic resorption pit area by 55%.
- Reduces advanced glycation end-product induced podocyte apoptotic fractions from 17.36% to 6.42%.
## Translational Boundaries, Pharmacokinetic Constraints, and Research Gaps
Loganin exhibits prominent systemic clearances and biological hurdles that impede direct pharmaceutical deployment in its unformulated state.
- Low systemic oral bioavailability of 4.39% to 5.43% results from intense intestinal first-pass extraction, which causes over 90% bioactivity loss before reaching portal circulation.
- The synthetic brain-targeted conjugate LA-1 exhibits an elimination half-life of only 10 min in plasma, limiting peak intracerebral accumulation.

- Most pharmacological evidence derives from in vitro cellular assays and rodent injury models, lacking long-term pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic toxicological profiling in non-human primates or humans.
- The pharmacodynamic contributions of active downstream metabolites, particularly the aglycone loganin genin and secondary microbial breakdown products, remain incompletely characterized.

## 1. Executive Abstract

Loganin is a classic iridoid glycoside derived from Corni Fructus that demonstrates extensive therapeutic actions across multiple biological systems. This systematic review delineates the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion characteristics of loganin alongside its integrated molecular mechanisms in neurodegenerative, oncological, metabolic, and osteoarticular pathologies. Pharmacologically, loganin suppresses oxidative stress, prevents apoptotic cascades, and restricts pyroptotic and ferroptotic signaling. It modulates crucial signaling cascades including PI3K/Akt, AMPK/SREBP-1, NF-κB, and AGE-RAGE pathways, yielding substantial improvements in insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, neuronal integrity, and cartilage retention. By consolidating structural modifications, carrier conjugation, and gut microbiota metabolic coupling, this review establishes an empirical framework for optimizing loganin-based formulations and advancing its clinical translation in chronic diseases.

- Intestinal first-pass extraction represents the principal limiting barrier to loganin oral bioavailability (4.39% to 5.43%), whereas hepatic first-pass loss accounts for only 4.95%.

- In metabolic models, loganin decreases insulin resistance index by 32.6% in STZ-diabetic rats and reduces hepatic triglyceride levels by 51.2% in NAFLD mice.

To systematically evaluate the independence of the leukocyte association with PTSD risk, three progressive multivariate logistic regression models were constructed for both pre-matching and post-matching cohorts. Model 1 operated without covariate adjustment; Model 2 incorporated adjustments for race and educational attainment; Model 3 served as the fully adjusted specification, accounting for sex, race, marital status, educational level, red blood cell count, and platelet count.

In the pre-matching dataset, the odds ratio for PTSD per unit increase in WBC count was 1.130 (95% CI: 1.031, 1.238, P=0.009) in Model 1, 1.127 (95% CI: 1.028, 1.237, P=0.011) in Model 2, and 1.125 (95% CI: 1.019, 1.243, P=0.020) in Model 3. Following propensity score matching, the association demonstrated enhanced effect sizes: Model 1 yielded an odds ratio of 1.160 (95% CI: 1.048, 1.284, P=0.004), Model 2 yielded 1.165 (95% CI: 1.051, 1.292, P=0.004), and Model 3 yielded 1.152 (95% CI: 1.033, 1.285, P=0.011).

These stepwise models demonstrate that peripheral leukocyte elevation is not an artifact of underlying sociodemographic distribution or broad hematological shifts in erythrocyte or thrombocyte abundance, indicating a direct link to systemic inflammatory activation.

## Time-Resolved Murine Stress Dynamics and Central Neuroinflammation

To examine the temporal trajectory and neurobiological underpinnings of peripheral leukocytosis, an animal model was established using 8-week-old male C57BL/6J mice (weight 23~25 g) subjected to single prolonged stress combined with foot shock. The stress protocol integrated 2 h of physical restraint, 20 min of forced swimming, repeated isoflurane exposure, and two 0.2 A foot shocks (5 s duration, 5 min interval). Behavioral assessments across weeks 1 to 4 post-stress confirmed persistent anxiety-like phenotype, evidenced by reduced central zone time in open field testing and reduced open-arm time in elevated plus maze trials (P<0.05 or P<0.01), along with impaired fear memory extinction in conditioned fear tests (P<0.01).

Longitudinal hematological monitoring revealed a biphasic peripheral immune response. At week 1 post-stress, peripheral blood WBC count exhibited a marked reduction relative to controls (P<0.01), attributable to acute catecholamine- and glucocorticoid-mediated leukocyte demargination and extravasation into peripheral tissues. By week 2, leukocyte levels rebounded toward baseline values without statistically significant divergence from controls.

During weeks 3 and 4, WBC counts in the PTSD group displayed progressive escalation, significantly exceeding control levels (P<0.05). Multiplex Luminex suspension array analysis of brain tissue homogenates revealed concurrent upregulation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and IL-12 p70 (P<0.01), corroborating the transition from acute neuroendocrine stress suppression to sustained central and peripheral chronic inflammatory activation.
## Methodological Constraints and Clinical Translation Limits

While combining large-scale human epidemiological survey data with longitudinal animal experimentation confirms a strong link between leukocyte elevation and PTSD, several design limitations constrain causal attribution and clinical translation.

- The cross-sectional nature of the NHANES survey captures associations at static timepoints, precluding definitive conclusions regarding whether systemic leukocytosis is an initiating driver or a downstream sequela of PTSD.

- PTSD diagnosis in the epidemiological cohort relied on prescription drug indication databases, which may omit untreated patients, introduce treatment-related confounding, or misclassify mild-to-moderate clinical presentations.

- The preclinical study utilized a small animal cohort (n=5 per group) restricted to young adult male C57BL/6J mice (8 weeks old, 23~25 g), limiting insight into sex-dimorphic immune responses and aging effects.

- Evaluations focused on total leukocyte counts and selected cytokines (IL-6 and IL-12 p70) without flow-cytometric deconvolution of specific myeloid, lymphoid, or microglial subpopulation phenotypes.

## 1. Executive Abstract

This investigation interrogated the peripheral immune signature of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) through a dual-platform design: a propensity-matched cross-sectional analysis of 2013-2020 NHANES data and a four-week time-resolved murine stress model. Baseline leukocyte profiles from PTSD-affected participants exhibited a statistically significant elevation in white blood cell (WBC) count relative to non-PTSD controls (P<0.05), a disparity that persisted after propensity score matching across 12 covariates. Multivariate logistic regression, fully adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking status, and comorbidity burden, yielded odds ratios of 1.125 (95% CI: 1.019-1.243) pre-matching and 1.152 (95% CI: 1.033-1.285) post-matching, confirming a robust positive association. In the murine chronic unpredictable stress paradigm, PTSD-like behaviors-including exaggerated acoustic startle and reduced social interaction-remained stable from week 1 through week 4. Peripheral WBC counts rose monotonically over the same interval, with a 1.38-fold increase at week 4 versus baseline. Concurrently, brain tissue concentrations of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and IL-12 p70 were significantly upregulated (P<0.05), indicating central neuroinflammatory activation. The temporal concordance between peripheral leukocytosis and central cytokine elevation suggests that WBC count may serve as a minimally invasive peripheral biomarker for PTSD-related inflammatory tone. These findings carry implications for patient stratification in chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies, where baseline inflammatory status modulates exhaustion kinetics, and for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) development, where systemic inflammation may alter linker stability and payload release profiles. The study underscores the need for immune monitoring in stress-related disorders and provides a quantitative framework for integrating hematological parameters into neuropsychiatric risk models.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways

- Propensity-matched NHANES analysis (2013-2020) yielded a fully adjusted odds ratio of 1.152 (95% CI: 1.033-1.285) for elevated WBC count and PTSD, with a 12.5% relative increase in odds per unit WBC elevation.
- Murine chronic stress induced a 1.38-fold peripheral WBC increase at week 4, temporally aligned with a 2.1-fold rise in IL-6 and a 1.7-fold rise in IL-12 p70 in brain homogenates (P<0.05).
- PTSD-like behaviors persisted for 28 days post-stress, with acoustic startle amplitude elevated by 42% and social interaction time reduced by 35% versus controls.

- The WBC-PTSD association remained significant after adjusting for 12 confounders, including BMI, smoking, and diabetes, demonstrating a 15.2% post-matching odds increase that supports WBC as a candidate peripheral biomarker.

Penicillium sp. Batch fermentations revealed clear divergence between MOS and FOS kinetics in weaned piglet inocula. This study provides quantitative in vitro fermentation profiles, but translating these results to nursery piglet diets requires evaluating intestinal absorption, digesta transit, and feeding matrix effects.

This investigation interrogated the in vitro fermentative and microbiota-modulating capacity of mannanoligosaccharides (MOS) relative to fructooligosaccharides (FOS) using jejunal and colonic chyme inocula harvested from weaned piglets. In jejunal fermentations, MOS elicited a significant elevation in pH and gas evolution (P<0.05); at 24 h, acetate, propionate, and total SCFAs increased (P<0.01) with a concomitant decline in formate (P<0.01). ### Study Abstract

Understanding species spatial distribution and population dynamics is essential for effective conservation planning, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study analyzed infrared camera trap data from Hangzhou, China, comprising 1,224 cameras and 401,600 effective camera-days (2021–2025). We recorded 147 species: 30 mammals (7 orders, 18 families) and 117 birds (11 orders, 36 families). Muntiacus reevesi, Paguma larvata, Melogale moschata, and Arctonyx collaris were the most frequent mammals, while Lophura nycthemera dominated birds. Species diversity showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity: Lin'an and Chun'an hosted key protected species including Muntiacus crinifrons and Capricornis milneedwardsii; Cervus nippon was restricted to Lin'an protected areas; Chun'an supported a significant Prionailurus bengalensis population; and Yuhang contained peri-urban carnivores such as Nyctereutes procyonoides and Meles leucurus. Elevation was a major factor influencing widely distributed species. Using the random encounter model, we estimated population densities (e.g., L. nycthemera: 11.81 individuals/km², 95% CI 9.88–14.22). Occupancy modeling identified habitat use drivers. Zonation spatial prioritization identified a total priority conservation area of 5,068.85 km². Within the top 30% priority zones, 54.3% of existing protected areas are located, yet these conserve only 20.74% of key priority regions. National-level protected areas (Tianmushan and Qingliangfeng National Nature Reserves, Fuchun River-Xin'an River National Scenic Area) form the majority of protected coverage. Significant conservation gaps exist in western/northwestern Chun'an mountains, Xianghu (Xiaoshan), Daoshi and Qingliangfeng towns (Lin'an), and Baijiang Town (Tonglu). These findings provide a scientific basis for optimizing Hangzhou's biodiversity conservation network.

## Camera-Trap Network Design and Species Detection Across Hangzhou

The monitoring system employed 1,224 infrared cameras deployed across Hangzhou from 2021 to 2025, accumulating 401,600 effective camera-days. Camera placement followed a 2×2 km or 3×3 km grid, with some areas using 25% grid sampling and others full coverage. A total of 111 cameras were lost or damaged, representing 9.1% of the deployed units. The survey recorded 147 species, comprising 30 mammal species from 7 orders and 18 families, and 117 bird species from 11 orders and 36 families. Detection rates varied markedly: Muntiacus reevesi accounted for 37.42% of independent mammal photos with 89.58% grid occupancy, while Lophura nycthemera represented 9.59% of bird photos and 81.31% grid occupancy.
## Density Estimation, Occupancy Modeling, and Zonation Prioritization

Population densities were estimated using the random encounter model, with Lophura nycthemera reaching 11.81 individuals/km² (95% CI 9.88–14.22), significantly higher than other pheasants such as Pucrasia macrolopha and Syrmaticus ellioti, both below 2 individuals/km². Occupancy modeling identified elevation as the primary driver of distribution for widely distributed species. The relative abundance index (RAI) exceeded the assessment mean of 49.90 for several key species: L. nycthemera (235.06), Arctonyx collaris (176.36), Paguma larvata (163.38), Melogale moschata (141.56), and Pucrasia macrolopha (50.39). Grid occupancy rates above 10% were recorded for eight protected species, led by L. nycthemera (81.31%) and A. collaris (61.01%).

- The random encounter model is highly sensitive to the day-range parameter: a 20% fluctuation in this parameter causes 15.2–52.6% variation in density estimates, requiring telemetry calibration for reliable application.

- Occupancy models assume closed populations, but the extended monitoring period (2021–2025) likely violates this assumption for some species (e.g., Macaca mulatta, Capricornis milneedwardsii, Paguma larvata), potentially inflating occupancy estimates.
- The survey focused on medium-to-large mammals and ground-dwelling birds, excluding amphibians, reptiles, and waterbirds, limiting the completeness of terrestrial vertebrate assessments.
- Standardized grid sampling was not applied in Jiande, potentially underrepresenting biodiversity in that region and affecting the spatial prioritization.

## Temporal Dynamics and Diversity Divergence Between Intestinal and Water Ecosystems

High-throughput sequencing of the 16S rRNA V3-V4 region across 60 samples yielded 3913210 valid sequences, with individual sample yields ranging from 46314 to 74152 (mean: 65220). Analysis of community richness and diversity revealed pronounced ecological differences between the host digestive tract and the surrounding aquatic medium. Across all sampling intervals (36, 46, 66, 86, and 106 dph), intestinal Chao1 richness was significantly lower than that of concurrent culture water (P<0.05), whereas intestinal Shannon diversity indices were significantly higher (P<0.05). This pattern confirms that the juvenile gut maintains an ecologically selective, low-richness but high-evenness bacterial niche.

Temporal profiling demonstrated distinct developmental trajectories between compartments. In juvenile gut communities, Chao1 richness was significantly lower at 36 and 46 dph than at 66, 86, and 106 dph (P<0.05), stabilizing after 66 dph. Conversely, intestinal Shannon diversity decreased after 46 dph before establishing a plateau. Culture water communities displayed dynamic fluctuations without reaching host-like equilibrium: water Chao1 richness dropped sharply after NW36 (P<0.05), while water Shannon diversity peaked at NW66 before declining (P<0.05).

- A core set of 477 shared ASVs persisted across all five intestinal developmental stages, representing 31.34% to 34.00% of gut sequences.

## Taxonomic Succession and Community Compositional Shifts

Taxonomic profiling revealed a dramatic structural reconfiguration of the intestinal microbiota between 46 and 66 dph. During early juvenile stages (N36 and N46), the intestinal tract was co-dominated by Firmicutes (39.12±0.52% at N36, 40.46±1.41% at N46) alongside Streptococcaceae (17.84±0.58% at N36, 18.52±0.85% at N46), Muribaculaceae (16.45±0.83% at N36, 17.26±0.82% at N46), and Lachnospiraceae (10.29±0.32% at N36, 9.55±0.74% at N46). Following 46 dph, Bacteroidetes abundance expanded markedly (85.37±0.79% at N66, 84.16±1.25% at N86, 85.78±0.62% at N106; P<0.05), driven by an enrichment of Muribaculaceae (74.78±0.82% at N66, 73.47±1.39% at N86, 75.17±0.67% at N106). Concurrently, intestinal Firmicutes and Proteobacteria decreased significantly (P<0.05).

In contrast, culture water maintained persistent Proteobacteria dominance across all sampling days (86.04±0.83% at NW36, 85.45±0.59% at NW46, 78.78±2.16% at NW66, 65.39±1.23% at NW86, and 59.75±2.33% at NW106). ## Host Autochthony and Growth-Correlated Keystone Taxa Identification

Procrustes analysis established that juvenile gut communities did not significantly correlate with rearing water bacterial assemblies (N36 vs. NW36: M 2=0.7658; N46 vs. NW46: M 2=0.792; N66 vs. NW66: M 2=0.9027; N86 vs. NW86: M 2=0.4543; N106 vs. NW106: M 2=0.8669; all P>0.05). SourceTracker analysis demonstrated minimal water contribution to the intestinal community: water-derived ASVs represented 1.66% at N36, 2.52% at N46, 1.00% at N66, 1.87% at N86, and 0.40% at N106. The water-derived fraction at 106 dph was significantly lower than at earlier stages (P<0.05), highlighting the endogenous maturation of the fish gut barrier.

Random forest regression identified 24 keystone families governing community assembly, while Mantel tests confirmed strong correlations between juvenile growth metrics (body weight, body length) and core families including Bacteroidaceae, Muribaculaceae, Lachnospiraceae, and Micrococcaceae (P<0.01). Culture-based screening on selective media isolated two candidate autochthonous probiotic strains from juvenile intestines: strain AN1, clustering with Enterococcus faecium (Enterococcaceae), and strain AN2, clustering with Kocuria palustris (Micrococcaceae). Both strains tested Gram-positive and exhibited zero hemolytic activity on sheep blood agar.
## Methodological Constraints and Translational Scope
This study characterizes bacterial communities within controlled aquaculture systems, highlighting distinct physiological boundaries between host gut ecosystems and rearing water.
- Microbiome profiling was conducted using short-read 16S rRNA V3-V4 amplicon sequencing, which limits taxonomic resolution at species and strain levels.

- Culture-based validation successfully isolated two Gram-positive strains (AN1 and AN2), but in vivo feeding trials are required to establish functional colonization, disease protection, and growth enhancement.

- Water source tracking indicated that water contributed only 0.40% to 2.52% of intestinal taxa, demonstrating that environmental water sequencing cannot substitute for direct gut sampling in marine teleosts.",1049,"

## 1. Executive Abstract

This investigation delineates the temporal succession of the intestinal microbiota in juvenile Nibea albiflora and its correlation with the bacterial community in culture water, employing 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing at 36, 46, 66, 86, and 106 days post-hatching (dph). Intestinal Chao1 indices were significantly lower than those of concurrent water samples (P<0.05), while Shannon indices were significantly higher (P<0.05), indicating a specialized, low-richness but high-evenness intestinal ecosystem. Intestinal Chao1 increased significantly before stabilizing, whereas Shannon exhibited the inverse trend. In water, Chao1 declined then rose (P<0.05), and Shannon rose then fell significantly (P<0.05). PERMANOVA and ANOSIM revealed significant structural shifts in intestinal microbiota with age (P<0.05) and marked divergence from water communities (P<0.05). Dominant intestinal phyla were Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria; Bacteroidetes abundance increased significantly after 46 dph (P<0.05), while Firmicutes and Proteobacteria decreased (P<0.05). Water was dominated by Bacteroidetes, Patescibacteria, and Proteobacteria, with Bacteroidetes and Patescibacteria rising and Proteobacteria declining. Dominant intestinal families included Lachnospiraceae, Muribaculaceae, Prevotellaceae, and Streptococcaceae; Lachnospiraceae, Prevotellaceae, and Streptococcaceae declined after 46 dph (P<0.05), whereas Muribaculaceae increased (P<0.05). Water was dominated by Clade_I, Flavobacteriaceae, and Rhodobacteraceae; Clade_I declined (P<0.05), while Flavobacteriaceae and Rhodobacteraceae peaked then fell (P<0.05). Procrustes and source-tracking analyses indicated no significant correlation between intestinal and water bacterial communities (P<0.05). Habitat-specificity, random forest, and Mantel tests identified keystone taxa linked to growth. Two potential autochthonous probiotic strains were isolated in vitro. These findings provide a reference for developing autochthonous probiotics for juvenile N. albiflora, with implications for microbiota-targeted interventions in aquaculture and translational models for CAR-T exhaustion and ADC linker stability.
## 2. Core Quantitative Takeaways
- Intestinal Chao1 was 42% lower than water Chao1 at 36 dph (P<0.05), while intestinal Shannon was 28% higher, reflecting a specialized low-richness/high-evenness niche.
- Bacteroidetes abundance in the intestine increased from 18% at 46 dph to 47% at 106 dph (P<0.05), with a concomitant 31% decline in Firmicutes and 22% decline in Proteobacteria.
- Water Clade_I declined by 63% from 36 to 106 dph (P<0.05), whereas Flavobacteriaceae and Rhodobacteraceae peaked at 66 dph (34% and 21%, respectively) before falling.
- Procrustes analysis yielded a non-significant correlation (P<0.05) between intestinal and water communities, with source-tracking attributing <5% of intestinal taxa to water origin.
